components.docs:
Displays one accessible image in a reserved frame, with an optional caption
and a fallback if the source is refused or fails to load.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
to show a photo, illustration, or diagram with a predictable
layout. Supply task-relevant alt text, or mark purely decorative media as
decorative. Set an explicit ratio when the layout must stay fixed.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
for a background decoration, a video, or an interactive
control. Use a separate control to open or otherwise act on an image.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text: caption - Optional visible context displayed below the media in a figcaption.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: figure - The figure containing the frame and optional caption.

docsTags.text: frame - The reserved media box and its shape and backing surface.

components.docs:
A non-interactive page-position indicator: one dot per position of a
bounded sequence, exactly one highlighted as current.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
show the current position within a bounded, sequential set of
peer views whose navigation lives elsewhere: carousel slides, unlabeled
onboarding steps, gallery pages. Wire `count` and `current` (1-based) to
the sequence the consumer renders and give it a `label` (required
authoring: assistive technology reads one graphic named
"<label>, <current> / <count>"). Below two positions an indicator carries
no information.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
section navigation (ki-tabs), task completion or loading
(ki-progress), labeled step flows (ki-stepper), interactive pagination
(ki-pagination — the indicator takes no focus and no input; navigation
belongs to the composing carousel's own controls), or conveying quantity
without a current position. Position
changes are never announced by the indicator itself (no live region): the
composing carousel owns announcements.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: indicator - The row container: layout and the token-driven gap.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: dot - Every dot: size, shape and color.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: dot-current - Additionally on the current dot: the highlight treatment.

usage.examples:
Two integers determine everything — one dot per `count` position with the 1-based `current` highlighted — and `label` names the sequence (the exposed name reads "<label>, <current> / <count>"):

```html
<ki-indicator label="Slide position" count="5" current="2"></ki-indicator>
```

Malformed declarations never break the row: `current` above `count` clamps to the last position, a non-numeric one falls back to the first, and an invalid `count` renders zero dots (an authoring mistake, not an error state):

```html
<ki-indicator label="Slide position" count="5" current="9"></ki-indicator>
<!-- fifth dot current -->
```

Drive it from the composing carousel by updating `current` (1-based); the highlight and exposed text follow immediately, and the indicator never announces changes (no live region) — announcements belong to the carousel:

```html
<ki-indicator id="gallery-position" label="Photo position" count="4" current="1"></ki-indicator>

<script type="module">
  const indicator = document.getElementById('gallery-position');
  indicator.current = 3;
</script>
```

props.name: count
props.docs:
Number of positions (non-negative integer): one dot renders per
position, in position order. A missing, non-numeric or negative value
renders zero dots — an authoring mistake by catalog guidance, never an
error state or a rendering failure (FR-002; empty ki-list precedent).
At most 20 positions render, and the catalog accepts no more: the
indicator serves a short sequence of peer views, 20 dots are the longest
row that fits a 320 CSS px viewport (the WCAG reflow width) in both
shipped themes, and one dot renders per position, so the bound also caps
the work a single node can demand. A larger value renders 20.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: undefined

props.name: current
props.docs:
The current position, 1-based to match the exposed position text
("2 / 5"). Exactly one dot presents the current appearance whenever
`count` >= 1: values above `count` clamp to the last position, values
below 1 and non-numeric values fall back to the first (FR-003). Updates
re-render in place — the highlight and the exposed text follow
immediately, re-applying the normalization (FR-004). The catalog accepts
1 to 20, the positions a bounded `count` can have.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: undefined

props.name: label
props.docs:
Accessible name of the sequence ("Slide position"). The exposed name
combines it with the wordless numeric position —
"<label>, <current> / <count>" — on a single non-interactive graphic;
without a label the name degrades to the bare position text (documented
as required authoring, FR-005). The label is never rendered visually
and position changes are never announced (no live region, FR-006).

parts.name: dot
parts.docs: Every dot: size, shape and color.

parts.name: dot-current
parts.docs: Additionally on the current dot: the highlight treatment.

parts.name: indicator
parts.docs: The row container: layout and the token-driven gap.

cssProperties.name: --ki-indicator-dot-block-size
cssProperties.description: dimension used by the indicator component for the resting dot block size: the 8px circle diameter measured in the State=inactive vector (the 16px frame height is row alignment, carried by the current dot).

cssProperties.name: --ki-indicator-dot-color
cssProperties.description: color used by the indicator component for the resting dot fill: Inverse_white/alpha_48 (Black/48 light, White/48 dark) — a declared a11y deviation from the MarsUI binding Inverse_white/alpha_18, which reads 1.53:1 light and 1.64:1 dark against the page; alpha_48 is the first step of the same ramp that clears the 3:1 FR-012 and WCAG 1.4.11 ask. The scheme flip rides the semantic layer.

cssProperties.name: --ki-indicator-dot-current-block-size
cssProperties.description: dimension used by the indicator component for the current dot block size: Space/3xl, the exact variable bound as the 16px height of the State=active pill (the full row line; declared family extension, design-extraction §Decisiones).

cssProperties.name: --ki-indicator-dot-current-color
cssProperties.description: color used by the indicator component for the current dot treatment: Inverse_white/alpha_48, the same step as the resting dots — the MarsUI State=active ring vector binds the variable of the resting fill, and its alpha_18 reads 1.53-1.64:1 against the page (declared a11y deviation, FR-012). Painted as the pill ring in onmars, where elongation carries the state; as the solid dot in themes that zero the hole.

cssProperties.name: --ki-indicator-dot-current-hole-block-size
cssProperties.description: dimension used by the indicator component for the block size of the transparent hole cut from the current pill: the 6px cutout height measured in the State=active vector; the ring width derives by construction as (current block size − hole block size) / 2 and a theme resolves it to zero for a solid dot (declared family extension, design-extraction §Decisiones).

cssProperties.name: --ki-indicator-dot-current-inline-size
cssProperties.description: dimension used by the indicator component for the current dot inline size: Space/10xl, the exact variable bound as the 32px width of the State=active pill — the MarsUI elongation lives here, never in an attribute (FR-007).

cssProperties.name: --ki-indicator-dot-current-radius
cssProperties.description: dimension used by the indicator component for the current dot shape: Radius/radius_round bound in Figma — the pill is a radius token, never an attribute (002 shape precedent).

cssProperties.name: --ki-indicator-dot-inline-size
cssProperties.description: dimension used by the indicator component for the resting dot inline size: Space/md, the exact variable bound as the 8px width of the State=inactive symbol; the painted circle is 8x8 centered in the 16px row line.

cssProperties.name: --ki-indicator-dot-radius
cssProperties.description: dimension used by the indicator component for the resting dot shape: Radius/radius_round bound in Figma — the round dot is a radius token, never an attribute (002 shape precedent).

cssProperties.name: --ki-indicator-gap
cssProperties.description: dimension used by the indicator component for the space between dots: Space/sm, the exact variable bound as the 6px gap of the composed Nav_indicator row (node 14195:5866, specs/024-ki-indicator/design-extraction.md).

cssProperties.name: --ki-indicator-motion-duration
cssProperties.description: duration used by the indicator component for the highlight transfer between dots: the Figma set documents no motion, so onmars resolves the single transition to the fast semantic duration (FR-008; disabled under reduced motion by construction).

cssProperties.name: --ki-indicator-motion-easing
cssProperties.description: easing used by the indicator component for the highlight-transfer transition (MarsUI standard curve; previously the UA default ease applied).

cssProperties.name: --ki-motion-duration-fast
cssProperties.description: Fast interaction transition duration.

cssProperties.name: --ki-motion-easing-standard-decelerate
cssProperties.description: Utility entrance curve. M3 md.sys.motion.easing.standard-decelerate. onmars: the MarsUI decelerate curve (ki.easing.out).

cssProperties.name: --ki-typography-family-body
cssProperties.description: semantic font family for typography family body.

components.docs:
A token-styled single-line text field with native input semantics.

Like a native field, it answers `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`,
`setCustomValidity(message)`, `validity`, `validationMessage` and
`willValidate` synchronously on a defined custom element.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
collect one line of free text from a person, always with a
visible `label`; choose the `type` and `autocomplete` that match the entry
purpose.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
multiline text, predefined choices, boolean state, numeric
stepper entry, or placeholder-only labeling.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text: start - Leading icon or text affix inside the field. Follows writing direction.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text:
end - Trailing icon or text affix inside the field. Follows writing direction.
A directly slotted AI label also describes the field as suggested by AI.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text:
action - One small submit action inside the field after the end adornment.
Use for one-field forms such as search or subscribe. Place a named
`ki-button size="sm" type="submit"` here, or wire a labeled
`ki-icon-button size="sm"` to request form submission. The action has its own tab
stop. Use the end slot for clear or reveal controls.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: count - Current character count and maximum at the end of the field message row.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text:
error - Error line shown in place of the help text while the field is invalid
after the person answered or submitted; a polite live region, starting with a
decorative error symbol.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: field - Enclosure wrapper for background, border, radius and focus ring.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: help - Help line under the field, read as the field's description.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: input - Internal native input that owns entry text, caret and selection.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: label - Visible label that provides the accessible name.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text:
label-hint - The `label-hint` text after the label text, inside the label and
part of the accessible name; rendered only while a hint is set.

docsTags.name: event
docsTags.text:
change - Fired when the user commits an edited value (native text-field
timing, such as on blur), composed across the shadow boundary; `value` is
already current when listeners run. When to use: react to a committed
value. When NOT to use: do not use it for per-keystroke updates; the native
`input` event carries those.

usage.examples:
A labeled field participating in native form submission (`label` is mandatory; it is the accessible name): ```html
Subscribe
``` Place a one-field form's only submit action inside the field. ```html
Search
``` The action has a separate tab stop. Enter in the entry also submits the form. For an icon-only action, give `ki-icon-button size="sm"` a `label` and call `form.requestSubmit()` from its click handler. Read-only and disabled are distinct states — read-only stays focusable and is submitted, disabled is neither: ```html ``` ## Appearance and character limits Set `appearance` to `outlined` for a full border or `filled` for a tinted surface with a bottom indicator. Both keep the label above the field. The default appearance follows the theme. Set `minlength` and `maxlength` to use the native input limits. With a maximum, `show-count` adds the current length to the field description and announces when the user reaches the limit. ```html EUR/ month ``` ## An error from the application Set `custom-error` to show the application's verdict on a submitted answer, such as a server-side check. The field is invalid, blocks its form and is announced as invalid at once. The person's next keystroke withdraws the error. Remove the attribute when a new attempt starts: setting the same text again while it is still set shows nothing. ```html ```

props.name: aiSuggestionText
props.docs:
Localized provenance description read alongside help or an error when
the end slot contains an AI label. Use this to translate the description.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: 'Suggested by AI'

props.name: appearance
props.docs:
Field appearance. `default` uses the current theme, `outlined` draws a
full border, and `filled` uses a tinted surface and bottom indicator.
The visible label stays above the field.
When to use: set an explicit appearance when fields must share a shape
across themes.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: 'default'

props.name: autocomplete
props.docs:
Native autocomplete detail token forwarded to the internal input.
When NOT to use: omit when no autofill entry purpose is known.

props.name: customError
props.docs:
An error of the application's own, such as a server-side or cross-field
verdict on the submitted answer ("Already registered"). While it holds
text the field is invalid, blocks its form, shows the text in place of
the help text at once and is announced as invalid. It stops counting at
the person's next change of the answer, or when the form is reset, so it
never blocks the corrected answer. It outranks `error-text` and an error
set with `setCustomValidity`.
When to use: report a verdict from a declarative spec, a live update or a
framework binding. Remove it when a new attempt starts.
When NOT to use: do not use it for `required` or other constraints the
field enforces itself; `error-text` words those. Setting the same text
again while the prop still holds it shows nothing: remove it first, then
set it again.

props.name: disabled
props.docs:
Prevents editing, removes the field from keyboard reach and exposes the
unavailable state through the internal native input.
When NOT to use: do not use disabled for readonly reference values.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: false

props.name: errorText
props.docs:
Message shown in place of the help text once the person's answer fails a
constraint (`required`, `type` or a length limit), and the field's `validationMessage`. Say
how to fix the answer ("Enter an email address like name@example.com").
Without it the browser's own message shows, in the browser's language. An
error set with `custom-error` or `setCustomValidity` outranks it.
When NOT to use: do not use it for server-side or cross-field errors; set
`custom-error` or call `setCustomValidity` for those.

props.name: helpText
props.docs:
One line of help under the field, read with it as its description: the
format expected, or why the answer is asked. While an error shows, the
error takes its place.
When NOT to use: do not repeat the label, and do not use it for error
messages; use `error-text`.

props.name: label
props.docs:
Visible label rendered next to the entry area and used as the accessible
name. This is mandatory for valid usage.
When NOT to use: never use `placeholder` as a label substitute.

props.name: labelHint
props.docs:
Short text shown after the label and read with it as part of the field's
name, so people know before submitting whether to answer: "(optional)" on
the few optional fields of a mostly required form, or "(required)" the
other way round, in the page's own language. It changes no validation;
set `required` for that, and keep the two consistent.
When NOT to use: do not put instructions or formats in it (use
`help-text`), errors (use `error-text`), or a repeat of the label.

props.name: maxlength
props.docs:
Native maximum length in UTF-16 code units. The input prevents user entry
past this limit.
When to use: cap the number of characters people can enter.

props.name: minlength
props.docs:
Native minimum length in UTF-16 code units for a nonempty user edit.
When to use: require a minimum number of characters in an answer.

props.name: name
props.docs:
Form-data key for the submitted value.
When NOT to use: omit when the field must not contribute named form data.

props.name: placeholder
props.docs:
Hint shown when the field is empty.
When NOT to use: do not use placeholder as the accessible name.

props.name: readonly
props.docs:
Makes the value focusable and selectable while rejecting edits.
When NOT to use: use `disabled` when the value must be unavailable and
excluded from forms.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: false

props.name: required
props.docs:
Marks the field as required for native constraint validation.
When NOT to use: do not use required on optional fields.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: false

props.name: showCount
props.docs:
Shows the current count and maximum next to the help or error text and
announces reaching or exceeding the limit. Requires `maxlength`.
When to use: give people feedback while writing to a limit.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: false

props.name: size
props.docs:
Token-backed field size (`--ki-input-{size}-*` tokens): the field box is
24, 32, 40, 48 or 56px tall in onmars, with its padding, radius, text and
icon box; the label and help text follow in three steps. An unrecognized
value matches no style rule and keeps the medium metrics.
When to use: match the size of the buttons and fields around it.
When NOT to use: do not pick a smaller size to fit a dense region or a
larger one for touch; declare `data-ki-density` on the region instead,
which composes with every size.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: 'md'

props.name: type
props.docs:
Entry kind with native single-line input semantics. Unknown runtime
values fall back to `text`; `number` is not a v1 input kind.
When NOT to use: use future numeric controls for locale-aware number entry.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: 'text'

props.name: value
props.docs:
Live text value. The attribute declares the initial default; the property
is the current value and programmatic assignments are silent.
Deviation from native (deliberate, research D2): assigning the ATTRIBUTE
programmatically also replaces the displayed value, silently — native
inputs would keep the user's dirty value. Form reset restores the
attribute's current value.
When NOT to use: do not observe user edits by polling; listen for `input`
and `change` (both re-dispatched composed across the shadow boundary).

slots.name: action
slots.docs:
One small submit action inside the field after the end adornment.
Use for one-field forms such as search or subscribe. Place a named
`ki-button size="sm" type="submit"` here, or wire a labeled
`ki-icon-button size="sm"` to request form submission. The action has its own tab
stop. Use the end slot for clear or reveal controls.

A directly slotted AI label also describes the field as suggested by AI.

from primary text, supporting text and optional media. Name interactive lists.

usage.examples: The list accepts only `ki-list-item` children (other children are unsupported); each item's default slot is the primary text line: ```html Ada Lovelace Grace Hopper Margaret Hamilton ``` Full item composition — `start` for leading media (decorative beside the visible name, so the avatar carries no `label`), `secondary` for supporting text and `end` for trailing meta: ```html Ada Lovelace Analytical engine programs Active Grace Hopper Compilers and COBOL 1906–1992 ``` ```html Account Name, email, password ``` ```html Ana Garcia Luis Perez ``` ```html Email digest Every Monday ```

usage.examples:
# Menu examples ## Row actions Register `ki-button`, `ki-menu`, `ki-menu-item`, `ki-menu-group`, and `ki-divider` when using the elements individually. ```html Actions Rename Duplicate Move to… Pin to sidebar Delete ``` ```js const menu = document.getElementById('row-menu'); menu.addEventListener('ki-select', ({ detail: { value, checked } }) => { dispatchRowAction(value, checked); }); ``` A plain action emits its value and closes the popup. A checkbox also emits its new checked state and keeps the popup open. A radio selection emits `checked: true`, clears its peer radios and closes the popup. Place independent radio sets in distinct groups. ## Account menu ```html

Ana García
ana@example.com

Profile Sign out ``` Give a glyph-only trigger an accessible name. Keep header content informational and put actions in `ki-menu-item`. A `start` slot can hold a decorative SVG or avatar. The application owns the shortcuts displayed by `shortcut`. With a filter, supply `filter-label` and optionally localize `filter-results-label`, retaining `{count}` where the number should appear.
usage.when-to-use:
# When to use Menu

Use Menu for commands on the same object, account actions, split buttons and
overflow actions. Keep destructive actions at the end after a divider. Pick
a select for a form value, links for navigation, or a dialog or page for
long action lists.

Supply a host-authored trigger with an ID in the same DOM tree. Bind the
catalog action on the menu's declared `ki-select` event. Application DOM
listeners can read the selected item's `value` and optional `checked` from
the event detail.

# ki-message examples ## User and event messages ```html Can I export my settings? Found the export guide ``` ## Assistant reply with an avatar and action The `author` prop names the article. Put formatted content in the default slot and application controls in `actions`. ```html Yes. Choose JSON from the export menu.
View source Settings export guide
``` ## Streaming reply Add `streaming` while the content is arriving, then remove it when the complete reply is available. Use a registered Markdown component in the default slot when your application displays formatted Markdown. ```html Choose the export format ``` ## Alternative replies ```html Choose JSON for a readable copy. ``` Handle `ki-branch-change` to show the requested alternative. Set `branchIndex` to `event.detail.index` when replacing the reply content. Set `actions-label` when the reply supplies a toolbar. The Conversation guide includes the complete Message actions recipe.

usage.examples:
# Using ki-mobile-nav

Use one bottom navigation bar for the three to five top-level destinations in
the phone layout. Place it after the content. The host reserves space in the
app shell so the last content can scroll above the links.

```js
import '@kimen/elements/icons/house';
import '@kimen/elements/icons/search';
import '@kimen/elements/icons/inbox';
```

```html
<main>
  <!-- App content -->
</main>
<ki-mobile-nav label="Main" variant="floating">
  <ki-mobile-nav-item href="/" icon-name="house" current>Home</ki-mobile-nav-item>
  <ki-mobile-nav-item href="/search" icon-name="search">Search</ki-mobile-nav-item>
  <ki-mobile-nav-item href="/inbox" icon-name="inbox" count="3">Inbox</ki-mobile-nav-item>
</ki-mobile-nav>
```

Omit `variant` for an edge-to-edge bar. When switching to TopNav or Sidebar,
use one app breakpoint to hide this bar and show the wider navigation.

usage.examples:
# ki-note usage

Place one or two lines of static context beside a control or inside a card.
Use `ki-alert` for results that need announcing, Toast for transient
confirmations and the field's `help-text` for field guidance.

```html
<ki-note>Only workspace owners can change billing details.</ki-note>
<ki-note tone="warning" size="sm">Changing the slug breaks existing links.</ki-note>
<ki-note tone="info" icon="false">This link is visible to everyone in the workspace.</ki-note>
```

## Decorative icon replacement

```html
<ki-note tone="info">
  <svg slot="icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2">
    <path d="M12 3v18M3 12h18"></path>
  </svg>
  Adding a billing contact gives them access to invoices.
</ki-note>
```

The words convey the message by themselves. The decorative icon is hidden
from assistive technology and adds no tab stop. Start warnings with the
consequence.

usage.examples:
# ki-number-input examples

## Quantity with bounds

```html
<ki-number-input label="Seats" name="seats" value="3" min="1" max="50" steppers required></ki-number-input>
```

## Plain field with a unit

```html
<ki-number-input label="Timeout" name="timeout" value="30" unit="seconds" min="0"></ki-number-input>
```

The form submits `timeout=30`.

## Percentage with localized editing

```html
<ki-number-input
  lang="de-DE"
  label="Discount"
  name="discount"
  min="0"
  max="1"
  step="0.005"
  value="0.125"
  format='{"style":"percent","maximumFractionDigits":1}'
></ki-number-input>
```

The editor displays `12,5` while focused and formats it as a percentage on
blur. The form submits `discount=0.125`.

## Text that is not a number

The field keeps text it cannot read as a number so the person can correct
it, shows its own message (`error-text`, else `invalid-number-message`) once
the person leaves the field or presses Enter, and stays invalid, so its form
cannot submit it. What it reports depends on what it held before:

- If it held a number, leaving the field fires one `change` and `value` is
  `undefined`, exactly as when the field is emptied.
- If it never held a number, it fires no `change`.

The event cannot tell an emptied field from an unreadable one; validity can:
`checkValidity()` answers `false` for unreadable text.

## An error from the application

Set `custom-error` to show the application's verdict on the submitted
number, such as a stock check. The field is invalid, blocks its form and is
announced as invalid at once. The person's next edit or step withdraws the
error. Remove the attribute when a new attempt starts: setting the same text
again while it is still set shows nothing.

```html
<ki-number-input label="Seats" name="seats" value="42" min="1" custom-error="Only 40 seats left."></ki-number-input>
```

## Custom-elements entry point

```ts
import { defineCustomElement } from '@kimen/elements/ki-number-input';

defineCustomElement();
const discount = document.querySelector('ki-number-input[name="discount"]');
if (discount) {
  discount.format = { style: 'percent', maximumFractionDigits: 1 };
}
```

props.name: customError
props.docs:
An error of the application's own, such as a server-side verdict on the
submitted number ("Only 40 seats left"). While it holds text the field is
invalid, blocks its form, shows the text in place of the help text at
once and is announced as invalid. It stops counting at the person's next
edit or step of the number, or when the form is reset, so it never blocks
the corrected answer. It outranks `error-text`.
When to use: report a verdict from a declarative spec, a live update or a
framework binding. Remove it when a new attempt starts.
When NOT to use: do not use it for `required`, the bounds or unreadable
text, which the field reports itself; `error-text` words those. Setting
the same text again while the prop still holds it shows nothing: remove
it first, then set it again.

components.docs: A declarative data option rendered by its owning `ki-select` or `ki-combobox`.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
declare one choice inside a `ki-select` or `ki-combobox`; its text is the
human-facing label and its `value` is the submitted value.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
`ki-option` standalone, authoring selection
on an option, or expecting it to paint its own row.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text: - Text label mirrored by the owning choice field.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text: start - Decorative content shown before the label in a combobox row.

usage.examples:
An option is meaningful only inside `ki-select`: it does not paint itself — the trimmed text is the visible label the select mirrors into its popup listbox, and `value` is what the form submits:

```html
<ki-select label="Language" name="language" placeholder="Choose a language">
  <ki-option value="en">English</ki-option>
  <ki-option value="es">Spanish</ki-option>
  <ki-option value="pt">Portuguese</ki-option>
</ki-select>
```

Omitting `value` submits the trimmed option text (native `<option>` parity); `disabled` options cannot be selected, are skipped by keyboard highlight, and are exposed unavailable by the select:

```html
<ki-select label="Priority" name="priority">
  <ki-option>Low</ki-option>
  <ki-option>Medium</ki-option>
  <ki-option disabled>Urgent</ki-option>
</ki-select>
```

Never author selection on the option — assign `ki-select.value` and the first matching option is selected silently:

```html
<ki-select id="language" label="Language" name="language">
  <ki-option value="en">English</ki-option>
  <ki-option value="es">Spanish</ki-option>
</ki-select>

<script type="module">
  document.getElementById('language').value = 'es';
</script>
```

usage.examples:
Use a named dialog popover for interactive filters. The host supplies the trigger in the same document or shadow tree. ```html Filters Open incidents ``` Use a toggletip to announce supplementary text and keep focus on the trigger. ```html About retention Logs are kept for 30 days. ``` Use a rich toggletip for an explanation with actions. Kimen follows the system setting.

Learn more ``` Use `open` to drive visibility and listen for `ki-open` and `ki-close` to observe it. In guarded catalog markup, bind actions to slotted controls. A trusted host can listen to the popover's two lifecycle events through the DOM.

components.docs:
A token-styled, non-interactive progress indicator for known or unknown
duration work.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
communicate advancement of an ongoing task such as upload,
download, installation or multi-step processing. Use `value`/`max` when
the completed fraction is known; use `indeterminate` when work is ongoing
but its duration cannot be measured, including loading-indicator use cases.
Choose `linear` in page flows and lists, and `circular` in compact or
centered placements. Always set `label` to what is progressing.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
static measurements within a known range such as disk
usage or scores (gauge/meter), step-by-step wizard navigation (stepper),
skeleton placeholders while content loads, or operations that finish in
under about one second.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: track - The full channel or ring: track ink and radius/stroke geometry.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text:
indicator - The advancing fill or arc: indicator ink and indeterminate
animation.

usage.examples:
A determinate task; `label` names what is progressing (without it the progressbar exposes no accessible name) and `value` is clamped to `0..max` for both presentation and ARIA:

```html
<ki-progress label="Uploading report.pdf" value="42"></ki-progress>
```

When the total is not 100, set `max`; non-finite, zero or negative totals normalize to `100`:

```html
<ki-progress label="Installing dependencies" value="3" max="8"></ki-progress>
```

Unknown-duration work sets `indeterminate` instead of a fabricated `value` (which is ignored while it is set); the motion is declared only when reduced motion is not requested:

```html
<ki-progress label="Contacting server" indeterminate></ki-progress>
```

`shape="circular"` fits compact or centered placements; unknown shape values render linear:

```html
<ki-progress label="Export progress" shape="circular" value="80"></ki-progress>
```

props.name: indeterminate
props.docs:
Unknown-duration mode. When set, no completed fraction or current value is
exposed. Its motion is declared only when reduced motion is not requested.
When to use: show ongoing work whose duration or total cannot be measured.
When NOT to use: do not use for known fractions; use `value` and `max`.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: false

props.name: label
props.docs:
Accessible name applied to the internal progressbar. Always set this to
what is progressing, such as "Uploading report.pdf". Without it the
element renders but exposes no accessible name, so the catalog contract
requires it.
When NOT to use: do not use a generic label such as "Loading" when the
task can be named more specifically.

props.name: max
props.docs:
Total amount. Non-finite, zero or negative values normalize to `100` for
presentation and ARIA.
When to use: set when a determinate task's total is not 100.
When NOT to use: omit for conventional percentage-style progress.

props.name: shape
props.docs:
Structural presentation. Use `linear` in page flows and lists; use
`circular` in compact or centered placements. Unknown values render linear.
When NOT to use: do not use shape to encode semantic status or task intent.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: 'linear'

usage.examples:
# PromptInput examples

Use a composer when a person can send a message to an assistant and stop its response. Provide a `label` even when there is a placeholder.

## Text and attachments

```html
<ki-prompt-input
  label="Message Kimen Assistant"
  placeholder="Ask anything, or drop a file"
  accept=".csv,.pdf,image/*"
  max-files="5"
  max-size="5000000"
></ki-prompt-input>
```

The file picker, drop area and clipboard share the same checks. `max-size` is the number of bytes allowed per file. An empty `accept` hides the attachment UI. The host receives a `ki-submit` event with `detail.text` and `detail.files`.

## Model selection and keyboard shortcuts

```html
<ki-prompt-input label="Message assistant" submit-on="mod-enter">
  <select slot="tools" aria-label="Assistant model">
    <option value="standard">Standard</option>
    <option value="careful">Careful</option>
  </select>
</ki-prompt-input>
```

In modifier mode, Control+Enter and Command+Enter send. Shift+Enter always inserts a newline. A model picker built with a menu can use the same slot. Read model selection from that control when handling `ki-submit`.

The application sets `status` to `submitted` while awaiting a response and to `streaming` when output begins. It handles `ki-stop` and sets `status` to `idle` when the response ends or stops.

components.docs:
A machine-scannable QR code that hands a declared value — a link, a
pairing payload — from the screen to a nearby camera, encoded locally
and restyled entirely through tokens.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
hand a URL or machine-readable payload from the screen to a
nearby camera device: login pairing, tickets and passes, "continue on
mobile" links, Wi-Fi sharing. Declare `value` (encoded verbatim, always
locally) and a purpose-stating `label` ("Open onmars.dev on your phone"),
and always offer the same payload through an accessible alternative next
to the code — a visible link or copyable text — because a QR code is only
useful to someone who can point a second device's camera at the screen.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
data the person must read on this same screen (render text
or a link), one-dimensional barcodes (out of scope), anything interactive
(a QR code is not a button — pair it with a real control instead), secret
values (anyone who can photograph the screen can decode them), or as the
sole carrier of the payload (the accessible alternative is mandatory
guidance). An always-empty ki-qr and a value beyond the ~2,331-byte
capacity are authoring mistakes: both render nothing, silently.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: code - The code tile: size, tile background and corners, quiet zone, module and finder shape/color.

usage.examples: A scannable link with a purpose-stating `label` (the accessible name) and the same payload offered as a visible link next to the code — the accessible alternative is mandatory, the code never travels alone: ```html onmars.dev ``` `value` is data, never behavior: it is encoded locally byte-for-byte and never interpreted, resolved, navigated to or fetched; non-ASCII text round-trips exactly: ```html ``` Malformed declarations never break a page: with no `value` (or one beyond the ~2,331-byte capacity) nothing renders and nothing errors: ```html ```

props.name: label
props.docs:
Accessible name stating the code's purpose ("Open onmars.dev on your
phone"). The component exposes exactly one non-interactive image named
by it, falling back to the encoded value when absent (FR-005) — never
an unnamed graphic. The label is never rendered visually, and naming
the purpose is what tells assistive-technology users to look for the
accessible alternative carrying the same payload (documented catalog
guidance, FR-013).

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: undefined

props.name: value
props.docs:
The exact text the code encodes — the single source of the content,
encoded locally as one UTF-8 byte segment at error-correction level M
(non-ASCII text additionally carries the UTF-8 ECI designator, so real
scanners decode the declared string rather than an ISO-8859-1
misreading), so an independent decoder recovers it byte-for-byte,
including non-ASCII text (FR-001), and no network request is ever made — the value is
data, never behavior: the component never interprets, resolves,
navigates to or fetches it (FR-002). Changes re-encode in place. When
absent, empty or beyond the capacity of the densest symbol (~2,331
bytes at level M), nothing renders and nothing errors (FR-003).

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: undefined

usage.examples:
Each option is a `ki-radio` child of a `ki-radio-group`; the slotted text is the option's accessible name and activation surface, and `value` is what the group submits when the option is selected:

```html
<ki-radio-group label="Delivery speed" name="delivery">
  <ki-radio value="standard">Standard (3–5 days)</ki-radio>
  <ki-radio value="express">Express (1–2 days)</ki-radio>
</ki-radio-group>
```

A disabled option cannot be selected or focused, and group arrow navigation skips it:

```html
<ki-radio-group label="Plan" name="plan" value="pro">
  <ki-radio value="free">Free</ki-radio>
  <ki-radio value="pro">Pro</ki-radio>
  <ki-radio value="enterprise" disabled>Enterprise (contact sales)</ki-radio>
</ki-radio-group>
```

Selection is never authored on the option — the parent group's `value` selects the matching option:

```html
<ki-radio-group label="Theme" name="theme" value="dark">
  <ki-radio value="light">Light</ki-radio>
  <ki-radio value="dark">Dark</ki-radio>
  <ki-radio value="system">Match system</ki-radio>
</ki-radio-group>
```

When NOT to use: do not use disabled as a temporary loading state.

When NOT to use: do not use `value` to author selection; set the group's

components.docs:
A token-styled radio group that owns selection, keyboard coordination and
form participation for slotted `ki-radio` options.

Like a native field, it answers `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`,
`setCustomValidity(message)`, `validity`, `validationMessage` and
`willValidate` synchronously on a defined custom element.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
a person must choose exactly one of a small set of mutually
exclusive options that should all be visible at once.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
many options or tight space (use `ki-select`), independent
on/off settings (use `ki-checkbox` or `ki-switch`), multiple selection, or
authored selection on options; set this group's `value` instead.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text: - `ki-radio` options. Document order is navigation order.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: label - Visible group label and accessible-name source.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text:
label-hint - The `label-hint` text after the group label text, inside the label
and part of the radiogroup's accessible name; rendered only while a hint is set.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: help - Help line under the options, read as the radiogroup description.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text:
error - Error line shown in place of the help text while the group is
invalid after the person submitted; a polite live region, starting with a
decorative error symbol.

docsTags.name: event
docsTags.text:
change - Fired once after the user selects a different radio, composed
across the shadow boundary; `value` is already current when listeners run.
`click()` on a `ki-radio` from a script selects it like a native radio: one
`input`, then one `change`.
When to use: react to the committed choice. When NOT to use: do not expect
it for programmatic `value` writes, which are silent.

usage.examples:
The group owns the `label` (mandatory; the radiogroup's accessible name), the form `name` and the selected `value`; user selection dispatches a composed `change` event, while programmatic `value` writes stay silent: ```html Standard (3–5 days) Express (1–2 days) Overnight ``` Without an initial `value` the group renders unselected and operable; `required` blocks form submission through the platform `valueMissing` validity until an option is chosen: ```html
Monthly Yearly Continue
``` A `disabled` group is skipped in Tab order and contributes no form entry; do not use it for pending or loading semantics: ```html Europe United States ``` When the question is already written on the page, name the group from it with `aria-labelledby` on the host and omit `label`, so the question is shown and read once: ```html

Which plan suits you?

Basic Pro ``` When the layout makes the question obvious but the group still needs its own name, `label-hidden` hides the label from view and from reading order; it stays the group's accessible name and is announced once: ```html Yes No ``` ## An error from the application Set `custom-error` to show the application's verdict on the submitted choice. The group is invalid, blocks its form and is announced as invalid at once. Choosing another option withdraws the error. Remove the attribute when a new attempt starts: setting the same text again while it is still set shows nothing. ```html Solo Team ```

props.name: customError
props.docs:
An error of the application's own, such as a server-side verdict on the
submitted choice ("This plan is sold out"). While it holds text the group
is invalid, blocks its form, shows the text in place of the help text at
once and is announced as invalid. It stops counting when the person
chooses another option, or when the form is reset, so it never blocks the
corrected answer. It outranks `error-text` and an error set with
`setCustomValidity`.
When to use: report a verdict from a declarative spec, a live update or a
framework binding. Remove it when a new attempt starts.
When NOT to use: do not use it for a `required` group left without a
choice; `error-text` words that. Setting the same text again while the
prop still holds it shows nothing: remove it first, then set it again.

props.name: disabled
props.docs:
Makes the whole group unavailable, skips it in Tab order and removes its
form entry.
When NOT to use: do not use disabled for pending/loading semantics.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: false

props.name: errorText
props.docs:
Message shown in place of the help text once a `required` group is left
without a choice, and its `validationMessage` ("Choose a plan"). Without
it the browser's own message shows, in the browser's language. An error
set with `custom-error` or `setCustomValidity` outranks it.
When NOT to use: do not use it for server-side or cross-field errors; set
`custom-error` or call `setCustomValidity` for those.

props.name: helpText
props.docs:
One line of help under the options, read with the group as its
description: what the choice decides. While an error shows, the error
takes its place.
When NOT to use: do not repeat the label, and do not use it for error
messages; use `error-text`.

props.name: label
props.docs:
Visible label and accessible-name source for the radiogroup.
When NOT to use: do not omit it unless the host's `aria-labelledby` names
the group from the page; a group with neither fails accessibility gates.

Naming from the page: set `aria-labelledby` on the host to the ids of
elements in the same document or shadow root, such as the heading that
already asks the question. The group then takes its name from them,
followed by its own `label` and `label-hint` when set. The ids are read
when the group renders and whenever the attribute changes.
When to use: the question is written on the page above the options; omit
`label` so the question is not shown, or read, twice.
When NOT to use: do not reference elements inside another component's
shadow root, which an id reference cannot reach.

props.name: labelHidden
props.docs:
Hides the `label` (and its hint) from view and from reading order while it
stays the radiogroup's accessible name, so a screen reader announces it
once, as the group's name.
When to use: the layout already makes the question obvious to sighted
people (a heading in a card, an icon row) but the group still needs a
name of its own.
When NOT to use: do not hide a label that repeats a question already on
the page; point `aria-labelledby` at that question instead. Do not hide
the only description of what a choice decides; that is `help-text`.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: false

props.name: labelHint
props.docs:
Short text shown after the group label and read with it as part of the
radiogroup name, so people know before submitting whether to choose:
"(optional)" on the few optional questions of a mostly required form, or
"(required)" the other way round, in the page's own language. It changes
no validation; set `required` for that, and keep the two consistent.
When NOT to use: do not put what the choice decides in it (use
`help-text`), errors (use `error-text`), or a repeat of the label.

props.name: name
props.docs:
Form-data key for the selected option's value. Omit when the group should
not contribute a form entry.
When NOT to use: do not put `name` on `ki-radio` options; their internal
native inputs are intentionally unnamed.

props.name: required
props.docs:
Requires one selected option for form submission. The group uses platform
`valueMissing` from its internal native radio inputs.
When NOT to use: do not use required when no answer is acceptable.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: false

props.name: size
props.docs:
Token-backed size of every `ki-radio` the group holds: the circle is 18
or 20px in onmars, and `sm` takes the smaller option label (13/20, 8px
away). The group decides for all its options; the group's own label,
help and error keep their size. An unrecognized value matches no style
rule and keeps the medium metrics.
When to use: match the size of the text and controls around the group.
When NOT to use: do not pick a smaller size to fit a dense region or a
larger one for touch; declare `data-ki-density` on the region instead,
which composes with every size.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: 'md'

props.name: value
props.docs:
Projection of the current selection. The initial attribute selects the
first matching option; unmatched values leave the group unselected and
operable. Assigning the property updates selection silently.
When NOT to use: never author selection on `ki-radio`; set this value.

usage.examples:
# Rating usage

## Display a review average

```html
<ki-rating readonly label="Average review score" value="4.3"></ki-rating>
```

The text reads 4.3. The glyphs fill to 4.5 and assistive technology receives one image named “Rated 4.3 out of 5”.

## Collect answer feedback

```html
<form>
  <ki-rating
    label="How useful was this answer?"
    name="usefulness"
    precision="0.5"
    required
  ></ki-rating>
  <button>Submit feedback</button>
</form>
```

A choice of 2.5 submits as `usefulness=2.5`. A form reset restores the starting value. Subscribe to `ki-change` for a user's changed choice and read its numeric `detail.value`.

## Use a different glyph

```js
import '@kimen/elements/icons/heart';
```

```html
<ki-rating
  label="How much did you enjoy the experience?"
  icon-name="heart"
  option-singular-label="{value} heart"
  option-label="{value} hearts"
></ki-rating>
```

usage.examples:
# Using ki-reasoning ## Show a plan while it develops ```html
  1. Check the inputs.
 ``` Add subsequent list items as the assistant produces them. The default state is collapsed. Set `open` to show the steps immediately. ## Show the elapsed time after completion ```html
  1. Check the inputs.
  2. Compare the available outcomes.
 ``` The summary reads “Thought for 12 seconds.” Omit `duration` if it is unavailable. ## Localize the summary ```html
  1. Revisar los datos de entrada.
 ``` ## Report disclosure changes in a guarded surface Declare the action in the surface and reference it on the disclosure. The renderer binds it to the catalog's `ki-toggle` event. ```json { "version": 1, "actions": ["record-plan-toggle"], "root": { "component": "ki-reasoning", "props": { "status": "done", "duration": 12000 }, "action": "record-plan-toggle", "slots": { "": ["Check the inputs and compare the outcomes."] } } } ``` ## Custom-elements entry point ```ts import { defineCustomElement } from '@kimen/elements/ki-reasoning'; defineCustomElement(); ```

components.docs:
A bounded scroll container that clips its content along one declared axis
and replaces platform scrollbar chrome with a token-resolved indicator.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
a bounded region inside a view whose content can outgrow it:
chat or message panes, code and log blocks, tag rows, sidebar navigation,
tall menus inside cards. Give it bounds (its size comes entirely from your
layout) and a `label` (required: the accessible name of the scroll
region). Scrolling stays native — wheel, touch, keyboard and indicator
drag operate the viewport directly.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
page-level scrolling (the browser's job), carousels or
paginated media (ki-carousel with ki-indicator), virtualized long
collections, multi-column tabular data, or nesting scrollers (v1
guarantees a single scroll axis per region). Cross-axis overflow is an
authoring mistake: the scroller scrolls its declared axis only and clips
the other — wrap or size content on the cross axis.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text: - The scrollable content: it keeps its own semantics and sizes the scroll extent along the declared axis.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text:
viewport - The scroll viewport: surface, focus ring and, as native
scrollbar chrome styled from `--ki-scroller-*` tokens, the indicator.

usage.examples:
A bounded vertical region; the scroller's size comes entirely from your layout and `label` (required) is the accessible name of the scroll region: ```html

March

Indicator fixes and token updates.

February

Initial scroller release.

 ``` `orientation="horizontal"` scrolls the inline axis instead; one axis per instance — the cross axis clips, so wrap or size content on it: ```html
MonTueWedThuFri
``` Scrolling stays native (wheel, touch, arrows, Page Up/Down, Home/End); the viewport joins the Tab order only while content actually overflows, and slotted content keeps its own semantics: ```html
  • Morning! Build is green.
  • Shipping the docs today.
 ```

props.name: label
props.docs:
Accessible name of the scroll region ("Release notes", "Chat
messages"). Assistive technology receives a `region` with this name
whose slotted content keeps its own semantics (FR-006). Documented as
required: a scroller without a label renders but exposes no accessible
name and fails the accessibility audit (015-ki-progress precedent).
The label is never rendered visually.

props.name: orientation
props.docs:
Declared scroll axis, mapping the design source's `Type` axis:
`vertical` (default) scrolls the block axis, `horizontal` the inline
axis. One axis per instance; the cross axis clips. A structural axis,
never appearance — thickness, shape and colors of the indicator are
per-theme `--ki-scroller-*` tokens. An unrecognized value matches no
style selector and no `horizontal` code path, so the scroller keeps
the default vertical behavior (fallback by CSS construction plus a
single strict comparison — no validation code, FR-002/FR-009).

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: 'vertical'

slots.docs: The scrollable content: it keeps its own semantics and sizes the scroll extent along the declared axis.

parts.name: viewport
parts.docs:
The scroll viewport: surface, focus ring and, as native
scrollbar chrome styled from `--ki-scroller-*` tokens, the indicator.

usage.examples:
# ki-segment examples

Place each choice directly in a `ki-segmented-control`. Give every choice a
distinct value, and set the selected value on the group.

```html
<ki-segmented-control label="Date range" value="week">
  <ki-segment value="day">Day</ki-segment>
  <ki-segment value="week">Week</ki-segment>
  <ki-segment value="year" disabled>Year</ki-segment>
</ki-segmented-control>
```

Use the `start` slot for a decorative icon. An icon-only option needs
`aria-label`, which also supplies its hover and focus tooltip when enabled.

usage.examples:
# ki-segmented-control examples

## Change a chart range

```html
<ki-segmented-control id="range" label="Chart range" value="week">
  <ki-segment value="day">Day</ki-segment>
  <ki-segment value="week">Week</ki-segment>
  <ki-segment value="month">Month</ki-segment>
</ki-segmented-control>
```

```js
import { defineCustomElement as defineControl } from '@kimen/elements/ki-segmented-control';
import { defineCustomElement as defineSegment } from '@kimen/elements/ki-segment';

defineControl();
defineSegment();

document.querySelector('#range').addEventListener('ki-change', ({ detail }) => {
  updateChartRange(detail.value);
});
```

## Give an icon-only option a name

```html
<ki-segmented-control label="View" size="sm" full-width>
  <ki-segment value="list">List</ki-segment>
  <ki-segment value="board" aria-label="Board">
    <svg slot="start" viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true">
      <path d="M2 2h4v12H2zm6 0h6v7H8z" fill="currentColor"></path>
    </svg>
  </ki-segment>
</ki-segmented-control>
```

The loader discovers the tooltip in the segment’s shadow root. With direct imports
or framework wrappers, register it before mounting an icon-only option.

```js
import { defineCustomElement as defineTooltip } from '@kimen/elements/ki-tooltip';

defineTooltip();
```

Supply a visible label when space permits. The icon-only option takes its
accessible name and hover or focus tooltip from `aria-label`. Keep slotted
content noninteractive.

components.docs:
A form-associated select-only combobox for choosing one option from
declarative `ki-option` children.

Like a native field, it answers `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`,
`setCustomValidity(message)`, `validity`, `validationMessage` and
`willValidate` synchronously on a defined custom element.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
choose exactly one value from a known closed list, especially
when there are roughly five or more choices or space is limited.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
`ki-radio-group` for a few always-visible choices,
`ki-input` for free or searchable text, `ki-checkbox`/`ki-switch` for
binary decisions, or multiselect and command menus.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text: - `ki-option` data children. They do not paint; rows are mirrored.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: label - Visible label and accessible-name source.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text:
label-hint - The `label-hint` text after the label text, inside the label and
part of the accessible name of the combobox and its listbox; rendered only while a
hint is set.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: trigger - Native button carrying the combobox role.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: value - Displayed selection or placeholder.

docsTags.name: part

docsTags.name: part

docsTags.name: part

error - Error line shown in place of the help text while the select is
invalid after the person chose or submitted; a polite live region, starting with
a decorative error symbol.

docsTags.name: event
docsTags.text:
change - Fired once after the user commits a different option, composed
across the shadow boundary and preceded by `input`; `value` is already
current when listeners run. When to use: react to the committed choice.
When NOT to use: do not expect it for programmatic `value` writes, which
are silent.

usage.examples:
Options are declared as `ki-option` children; the option text is the visible label and `value` is the submitted value:

```html
<ki-select label="Country" name="country" placeholder="Choose a country">
  <ki-option value="es">Spain</ki-option>
  <ki-option value="fr">France</ki-option>
  <ki-option value="pt">Portugal</ki-option>
</ki-select>
```

An option without `value` submits its trimmed label text, and `required` blocks submission while empty:

```html
<form>
  <ki-select label="Team size" name="size" required>
    <ki-option>1-10</ki-option>
    <ki-option>11-50</ki-option>
    <ki-option disabled>51+</ki-option>
  </ki-select>
  <ki-button variant="primary">Continue</ki-button>
</form>
```

## An error from the application

Set `custom-error` to show the application's verdict on the submitted
choice, such as a server-side check. The select is invalid, blocks its form
and is announced as invalid at once. Choosing another option withdraws the
error. Remove the attribute when a new attempt starts: setting the same text
again while it is still set shows nothing.

```html
<ki-select label="Country" name="country" value="ch" custom-error="We do not ship to Switzerland yet.">
  <ki-option value="es">Spain</ki-option>
  <ki-option value="ch">Switzerland</ki-option>
</ki-select>
```

props.name: customError
props.docs:
An error of the application's own, such as a server-side verdict on the
submitted choice ("We do not ship there"). While it holds text the select
is invalid, blocks its form, shows the text in place of the help text at
once and is announced as invalid. It stops counting when the person
chooses another option, or when the form is reset, so it never blocks the
corrected answer. It outranks `error-text` and an error set with
`setCustomValidity`.
When to use: report a verdict from a declarative spec, a live update or a
framework binding. Remove it when a new attempt starts.
When NOT to use: do not use it for a `required` select left without a
choice; `error-text` words that. Setting the same text again while the
prop still holds it shows nothing: remove it first, then set it again.

props.name: disabled
props.docs:
Prevents opening, removes the trigger from keyboard reach, and excludes
the select from form submission.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: false

props.name: errorText
props.docs:
Message shown in place of the help text once a `required` select is left
without a choice, and its `validationMessage` ("Choose a country").
Without it the browser's own message shows, in the browser's language. An
error set with `custom-error` or `setCustomValidity` outranks it.
When NOT to use: do not use it for server-side or cross-field errors; set
`custom-error` or call `setCustomValidity` for those.

props.name: helpText
props.docs:
One line of help under the trigger, read with it as the combobox
description: what the choice decides. While an error shows, the error
takes its place.
When NOT to use: do not repeat the label, and do not use it for error
messages; use `error-text`.

props.name: label
props.docs:
Visible label and accessible-name source for the combobox trigger.
When NOT to use: do not omit it; unlabeled selects are invalid usage.

props.name: labelHint
props.docs:
Short text shown after the label and read with it as part of the
combobox name, so people know before submitting whether to choose:
"(optional)" on the few optional fields of a mostly required form, or
"(required)" the other way round, in the page's own language. It changes
no validation; set `required` for that, and keep the two consistent.
When NOT to use: do not put instructions in it (use `help-text`), errors
(use `error-text`), or a repeat of the label.

props.name: name
props.docs:
Form-data key used when a selected option contributes its value.
When NOT to use: omit it when the select should not submit data.

props.name: placeholder
props.docs:
Text shown while no option is selected.
When NOT to use: do not use it as a replacement for `label`.

props.name: required
props.docs:
Requires a non-empty submitted value. The platform validation message is
donated by a hidden native select.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: false

props.name: size
props.docs:
Token-backed trigger size (`--ki-select-{size}-*` tokens): the trigger is
24, 32, 40, 48 or 56px tall in onmars, with its padding, radius, text and
indicator; the label and help text follow in three steps. The listbox
and its options keep their size. An unrecognized value matches no style
rule and keeps the medium metrics.
When to use: match the size of the fields around it.
When NOT to use: do not pick a smaller size to fit a dense region or a
larger one for touch; declare `data-ki-density` on the region instead,
which composes with every size.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: 'md'

Live projection of the selected option value, or `""` when unselected.
Assigning it selects the first matching option silently; the attribute is
the reset/default declaration and is not updated by user commits.

while it loads. Give the surrounding region an accessible name and set
its aria-busy state. Show the skeleton after about 300 ms of waiting.

or interactive control. Put content and loading feedback in the caller's region.

props.name: animated
props.docs:
Sweep a highlight while the user permits motion. Set false to use a static
placeholder. Shimmer also stops under reduced motion and forced colours.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: true

props.name: blockSize
props.docs:
CSS length for the block axis. For text, this is the height of each line.
Use it to reserve the height of the content that will replace the shape.

props.name: inlineSize
props.docs:
CSS length for the inline axis. Use it to match a fixed content width.
Text and rectangles otherwise fill available inline space.

props.name: lines
props.docs:
Number of text lines. Use a whole number from 1 to 20 for the expected
paragraph length. Extra lines are ignored for circles and rectangles.

usage.examples:
# Slider examples

Import the element, the token core and the slider's token sheet before
mounting the examples.

```js
import '@kimen/tokens/css/core';
import '@kimen/tokens/css/ki-slider';
import { defineCustomElement } from '@kimen/elements/ki-slider';

defineCustomElement();
```

```html
<form>
  <ki-slider label="Volume" name="volume" help-text="Playback level"
    min="0" max="100" step="1" value="60" marks="5" format="percent"></ki-slider>
  <ki-slider label="Price per night" name="price" range
    value="20,80" format="currency" currency="EUR"></ki-slider>
  <button type="reset">Reset</button>
</form>

<ki-slider label="Exposure" centered min="-50" max="50" value="-20"></ki-slider>
<ki-slider label="Bass" orientation="vertical" max="10" value="4"></ki-slider>
```

A named slider contributes one form entry. The form above starts with
`volume=60` and `price=20,80`. Range values always run from lower to upper.
The closest `lang` controls the display format. Localize the thumb suffixes
through `minimum-label` and `maximum-label`.

```js
const volume = document.querySelector('ki-slider[name="volume"]');
volume.addEventListener('input', () => previewVolume(volume.value));
volume.addEventListener('change', () => saveVolume(volume.value));
```

The neutral catalog exposes the `change` action event. Bind it to a declared
action to receive the current value on commit.

# Using Sources Put a citation immediately after the clause it supports. Put the source definitions directly inside the corresponding disclosure. The list shows sources in order of first citation and adds uncited sources in declaration order. ```html

The study design explains the results.

``` Use `open` to start with the list expanded. Use unique source identifiers within each document or shadow root. Hover or focus a citation to see its title and hostname. Activate it to expand the list and focus the title link. The card links can be used independently of the inline markers. When importing individual elements, register all three tags with their respective `defineCustomElement()` functions. Use `citationRef` and `sourceTitle` as component props in JSX. In a guarded spec, use keys `ref`, `source-id`, `title` and `href` on their respective nodes. Put the citation in a `div` primitive if it shares a line with text. Provide the local language through `label-template`, `source-count-label`, and `sources-count-label`. Titles and snippets are plain text. HTTP(S) URLs and relative web references work in authored HTML. Guarded specs also follow the application's allowed-origin policy.

usage.examples:
# ki-spinner examples

## Inline save status

Insert the spinner when the save begins. Remove it when the save ends.

```html
<ki-spinner size="sm" label="Saving changes…" show-label></ki-spinner>
```

## Assistant status

Use a visually hidden label when the surrounding UI already describes the
activity.

```html
<ki-spinner variant="dots" label="Assistant is thinking"></ki-spinner>
```

## Custom-elements entry point

```ts
import { defineCustomElement } from '@kimen/elements/ki-spinner';

defineCustomElement();
```

usage.examples:
# Stat

Use one stat for one key number. Choose the preference for the metric. Here,
the render time went down and the change is favorable.

```html
<ki-stat
  label="Median render time"
  value="84"
  unit="ms"
  delta="-9"
  delta-label="vs last week"
  direction="lower-is-better"
></ki-stat>
```

For a percentage comparison beside a count, set `deltaFormat` as a property.
Percent formatting takes a fraction, so 0.12 reads as 12%.

```html
<ki-stat id="active-surfaces" label="Active surfaces" value="1284" delta="0.12" delta-label="vs last week"></ki-stat>
```

```js
document.querySelector('#active-surfaces').deltaFormat = { style: 'percent' };
```

With no `delta`, the card shows the current value alone. For a trend that carries
no judgment, use `direction="neutral"`. For an informative sparkline, give the
chart a text equivalent through its own HTML semantics.

```html
<ki-stat label="Sales" value="750">

components.docs: A tiny, non-interactive status dot that marks the state of a nearby item.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
mark a state with minimal footprint adjacent to (or overlaid
on) the item it describes: presence on an avatar, health of a service
list entry, connection state in a toolbar. Label it (`label`) or pair it
with adjacent visible text — color is never the only carrier of the
meaning (WCAG 1.4.1).

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
short labeled status text (that pill is ki-badge — this dot
never renders text), notification counters or the overlay attachment
mechanism (a future, separate nav-badge concern), messages that need
attention or announcement (ki-alert — the dot has no live region),
progress or loading (ki-progress). An unlabeled dot without adjacent
visible text is an authoring mistake (WCAG 1.4.1).

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: dot - The dot itself: size, tone fill, radius, ring and effects.

usage.examples:
`tone` declares semantic intent and `label` exposes the dot as a named non-interactive image; an unrecognized tone keeps the neutral appearance: ```html ``` Without a `label` the dot is decorative and contributes nothing to the accessibility tree — adjacent visible text must then carry the meaning (color is never the only carrier, WCAG 1.4.1): ```html

Online

``` `ring` keeps the dot distinguishable over media; positioning the overlay is the consumer's layout concern, and the ring never shifts layout: ```html

props.name: label
props.docs:
Accessible name for the state ("Online", "Build failing"). With a
label the dot is exposed to assistive technology as a named
non-interactive image (role `img`); without one it is decorative and
contributes nothing to the accessibility tree — the meaning must then
live in adjacent visible text (FR-003, FR-008). The label is never
rendered visually: visible status text belongs to ki-badge. Runtime
changes are not announced (no live region, FR-005).

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: undefined

props.name: ring
props.docs:
Draws a separating ring around the dot for placement over media (an
avatar photo), keeping it distinguishable from the pixels beneath. A
per-instance functional axis — MarsUI ships Outline=True|False as
sibling variants under one theme (recorded deviation from the 002
token-only rule) — while ring width and color stay per-theme
`--ki-status-ring-*` tokens. The ring paints outside the dot's box and
never shifts layout.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: false

props.name: tone
props.docs:
Semantic intent, never appearance: each tone resolves its fill from
the per-theme `--ki-status-{tone}-color` tokens. An unrecognized value
matches no style selector, so the dot keeps the neutral appearance
(fallback by CSS construction — no validation code, FR-007).

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: 'neutral'

cssProperties.name: --ki-status-danger-color
cssProperties.description: color used by the status component for the danger tone fill: Surface/danger_med_em, the exact variable bound to the Type=danger Status variant (Danger/500).

cssProperties.name: --ki-status-info-color
cssProperties.description: color used by the status component for the info tone fill: Surface/info_high_em (Info/600 light, Info/400 dark) — one step above the med-em 500 pattern the success and danger tones follow, because Info/500 reads 2.29:1 on the light page and WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1 of the dot (FR-008). No Figma Status variant ships an info Type, so the fill remains an extrapolation onto the Info ramp (001 contract, 010/015 precedent) declared for founder ratification.

cssProperties.name: --ki-status-neutral-color
cssProperties.description: color used by the status component for the neutral tone fill: ki.outline.control, the semantic 3:1 non-text floor (Black/48 light, White/48 dark; md.sys.color.outline in material3) — a declared a11y deviation from the MarsUI binding Surface/disabled_high_em (Gray/500 light, White/32 dark), which reads 2.10:1 and 2.78:1 against the page where WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1 of the dot (FR-008). MarsUI's disabled gray still maps to the charter neutral tone (spec Assumptions).

cssProperties.name: --ki-status-radius
cssProperties.description: dimension used by the status component for the dot shape: Radius/radius_round bound in Figma — the round dot is a radius token, never an attribute (002 shape precedent).

cssProperties.name: --ki-status-ring-color
cssProperties.description: color used by the status component for the separating ring: Outline/inverse_black, the exact variable bound to Outline=True variants — white over light surfaces, black over dark ones, so the ring reads as a cutout from the underlying media (FR-002).

cssProperties.name: --ki-status-ring-width
cssProperties.description: dimension used by the status component for the separating ring: the 2px stroke on every Outline=True Status variant (FR-002).

cssProperties.name: --ki-status-shadow
cssProperties.description: shadow used by the status component for the dot effects: the exact MarsUI pair on every Status variant — e1 drop (0/1/1/-0.5 in the scheme shadow color) plus inner White/12 highlight (0/3/3), i.e. Component_effect/primary_default's box-shadow layers, flat in onmars v2. Its backdrop blur is not applied: a 4px dot has nothing to blur (brief §5 perf note).

cssProperties.name: --ki-status-size
cssProperties.description: dimension used by the status component for the dot: the MarsUI 4px dot, Space/xs bound to every Status variant (specs/021-ki-status/design-extraction.md). One size per theme, never an attribute (FR-006).

cssProperties.name: --ki-status-success-color
cssProperties.description: color used by the status component for the success tone fill: Surface/success_med_em, the exact variable bound to the Type=success Status variant (Success/500).

cssProperties.name: --ki-status-warning-color
cssProperties.description: color used by the status component for the warning tone fill: Text/warning_high_em (Warning/800 light, Warning/300 dark) — a declared a11y deviation from the MarsUI binding Surface/warning_med_em (Warning/500), which reads 1.92:1 on the light page. No warning surface step clears the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 asks of the dot (Warning/600 reads 2.33:1), so the fill takes the warning ink that is legible on the page (FR-008).

usage.examples:
# Stepper examples

## Setup wizard

```html
<ki-stepper label="Setup progress">
  <ki-step state="done" href="/setup/account">Account</ki-step>
  <ki-step state="done">Workspace</ki-step>
  <ki-step state="current">Invite team</ki-step>
  <ki-step>Review</ki-step>
</ki-stepper>
```

At under 22rem of available inline size, the horizontal stepper shows
**Step 3 of 4**. Activate the summary to open the ordered list and return
to the Account step.

## Vertical setup guide

```html
<ki-stepper label="Publish a surface" orientation="vertical">
  <ki-step state="done">Connect the repository</ki-step>
  <ki-step state="current">Choose a theme</ki-step>
  <ki-step state="error" description="Check the repository permissions.">Run checks</ki-step>
  <ki-step description="Publish when the checks pass.">Publish</ki-step>
</ki-stepper>
```

## Localized status and summary

```html
<ki-stepper
  label="Avance de la configuración"
  done-label="Completado"
  current-label="Actual"
  upcoming-label="Sin empezar"
  error-label="Error"
  summary-label="Paso {current} de {total}"
  count-label="Pasos ({total})"
>
  <ki-step state="done">Cuenta</ki-step>
  <ki-step state="current">Equipo</ki-step>
  <ki-step>Revisión</ki-step>
</ki-stepper>
```
