components.docs:
A token-styled switch for immediate on/off settings.

Like a native field, it answers `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`,
`setCustomValidity(message)`, `validity`, `validationMessage` and
`willValidate` synchronously on a defined custom element.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
binary settings whose change takes effect immediately, always
with a slotted label.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
selections collected for later form submission; use
ki-checkbox for recorded choices, ki-radio-group for mutually exclusive
choices, and ki-button for actions.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text: - Label content. This is the accessible name source.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text: end - Trailing value outside the label.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: track - On/off channel.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: thumb - Traveling handle.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: label - Label wrapper around the default slot.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: help - Help line under the switch, read as its description.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text:
error - Line that shows, in place of the help text, an error the
application set with `setCustomValidity` once the form is submitted; a polite
live region, starting with a decorative error symbol.

docsTags.name: event
docsTags.text:
change - Fired once after a user toggle commits, composed across the shadow
boundary; `checked` is already current when listeners run. `click()` from a
script, or a page `<label>` for the switch, toggles it like a native
checkbox: one `input`, then one `change`. When to use:
apply the on/off effect. When NOT to use: do not expect it for programmatic
`checked` writes, which are silent.

usage.examples:
The slotted label provides the accessible name. ```html Autosave Desktop notifications ``` While on, a named switch contributes `name`/`value` to native form data (`on` when `value` is omitted, checkbox parity); while off it contributes nothing: ```html
Usage analytics
``` User toggles dispatch composed `input` and `change` events — apply the setting immediately, a switch never waits for a submit; `disabled` preserves the current state while removing the switch from keyboard reach and form data: ```html Beta features (unavailable on this plan) ``` ## An error from the application Set `custom-error` to show the application's verdict on a setting it could not apply. The switch is invalid, blocks its form and is announced as invalid at once. Toggling it withdraws the error. Remove the attribute when a new attempt starts: setting the same text again while it is still set shows nothing. ```html Two-step sign-in ``` ## Settings row Stretch the switch in a grid or set `display: block` on the host. Put the current value in `slot="end"`. The default slot supplies the switch name and the value sits at the inline end. Update the value when the switch changes. ```html Email notificationsOn ```

props.name: checked
props.docs:
Live on/off state.
When to use: set the initial on state for a setting that applies
immediately.
When NOT to use: do not use a switch for choices saved only on submit;
use ki-checkbox for that pattern.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: false

props.name: customError
props.docs:
An error of the application's own, such as a server-side verdict on the
submitted setting ("Two-step sign-in needs a phone number"). While it
holds text the switch is invalid, blocks its form, shows the text in
place of the help text at once and is announced as invalid. It stops
counting when the person toggles the switch, or when the form is reset,
so it never blocks the corrected answer. It outranks an error set with
`setCustomValidity`.
When to use: report a verdict from a declarative spec, a live update or a
framework binding. Remove it when a new attempt starts.
When NOT to use: do not use it for help that is not an error; use
`help-text`. Setting the same text again while the prop still holds it
shows nothing: remove it first, then set it again.

props.name: disabled
props.docs:
Prevents toggling, removes the switch from keyboard reach, excludes it
from form data, and exposes the unavailable state to assistive technology.
When to use: make a setting temporarily unavailable while preserving its
current state.
When NOT to use: do not use disabled for pending or loading states.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: false

props.name: helpText
props.docs:
One line of help under the switch, read with it as its description: what
turning it on changes.
When NOT to use: do not repeat the label. A switch has no constraint of
its own, so it takes no error text; an error the application sets with
`custom-error` or `setCustomValidity` shows in this line's place.

props.name: name
props.docs:
Form-data key contributed while the switch is on.
When to use: include the immediate setting in native form data when on.
When NOT to use: omit when no form entry should be submitted.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: undefined

props.name: size
props.docs:
Token-backed size: the track is 32 x 18, 40 x 22, 48 x 26 or 56 x 32px in
onmars (`xl` is the design's mobile size), with its thumb. `sm` also takes
the smaller label (13/20, 8px away). An unrecognized value matches no
style rule and keeps the medium metrics.
When to use: match the size of the text and controls around it.
When NOT to use: do not pick a smaller size to fit a dense region or a
larger one for touch; declare `data-ki-density` on the region instead,
which composes with every size.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: 'md'

props.name: value
props.docs:
Form-data value submitted while on. Omit for native checkbox parity: the
submitted value defaults to `on`.
When to use: submit a domain-specific value instead of the default `on`.
When NOT to use: do not set a value to represent off; off contributes
nothing.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: 'on'

components.docs: One selectable tab inside a `ki-tabs` view switcher.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
label one peer content view inside `ki-tabs`, with optional
decorative `icon` and `start` or `end` slot media.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
standalone, for form value
selection, or for page navigation; use the parent group's `value` instead
of authoring `selected`.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text: - Required visible text label and accessible name source.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text: icon - Decorative SVG. Supply visible text in the default slot.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text: start - Leading icon or media. Follows writing direction.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text: end - Trailing icon or media. Follows writing direction.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: tab - Tab surface.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: indicator - Decorative selected-tab marker.

usage.examples: A tab's default slot is its label and accessible name source; `value` pairs it with the `ki-tab-panel` sharing the same value inside a `ki-tabs` group: ```html Profile Privacy Profile settings Privacy settings ``` The `start` and `end` slots hold leading and trailing icons or media (they follow writing direction); keep decorative media `aria-hidden`: ```html ✉ All mail Unread Every conversation. Unread conversations only. ``` `disabled` excludes the tab from selection by every modality, and `selected` is output-only state written by the group — set the group's `value` instead of authoring it: ```html Commits Releases Commit history Published releases ``` For a decorative SVG, use the `icon` slot and give the tab a visible text label in the default slot. components.docs: One content view paired with a `ki-tab` inside `ki-tabs`.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
hold the content for one peer tab view, sharing `value` with
its `ki-tab`.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
standalone, as lazy mounting, or for page
navigation; orphan and duplicate panels are hidden by the parent group.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text: - Panel content.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: panel - Panel surface.

usage.examples:
A panel is visible only while the `ki-tab` sharing its `value` is selected; the default slot holds the content:

```html
<ki-tabs label="Documentation" value="guide">
  <ki-tab value="guide">Guide</ki-tab>
  <ki-tab value="reference">Reference</ki-tab>
  <ki-tab-panel value="guide">Step-by-step instructions.</ki-tab-panel>
  <ki-tab-panel value="reference">Complete API tables.</ki-tab-panel>
</ki-tabs>
```

Panels hold arbitrary content, form controls included; every panel mounts eagerly (no lazy mounting exists):

```html
<ki-tabs label="Account" value="contact">
  <ki-tab value="contact">Contact</ki-tab>
  <ki-tab value="password">Password</ki-tab>
  <ki-tab-panel value="contact">
    <ki-input label="Work email" name="email" type="email"></ki-input>
  </ki-tab-panel>
  <ki-tab-panel value="password">Password change form.</ki-tab-panel>
</ki-tabs>
```

The first panel with a given `value` owns it — duplicate or orphan panels stay hidden without error:

```html
<ki-tabs label="Report" value="summary">
  <ki-tab value="summary">Summary</ki-tab>
  <ki-tab-panel value="summary">Quarterly totals.</ki-tab-panel>
  <ki-tab-panel value="detail">Never shown: no tab shares this value.</ki-tab-panel>
</ki-tabs>
```

components.docs: A scrollable frame for a native data table with optional sorting and selection.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
Show records with shared fields that people compare, scan or sort.
Supply a native caption, column headers with scope="col" and record headers
with scope="row". Mark numeric cells with data-numeric and secondary cells
with data-meta. The host application supplies the native table markup.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
Lay out a screen, show a short one-line list, or present the
name-value details of one record. Use CSS grid, ki-list or a description list.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text:
- One native light-DOM table with a caption, head and body. Use data-sort
on sortable headers and data-key on each record available for selection.

usage.examples:
# Table examples Wrap one native table and keep the caption, column scope and row scope in the markup. A selected row's `data-key` identifies its record after sorting or replacement. ```html
Services
Name Status Runs
Billing API Ready 64
Search index Slow 18
``` With individual imports or a framework wrapper, register `ki-checkbox` when using `selectable`. The loader defines the checkbox when the table draws it. ```js import { defineCustomElement as defineTable } from '@kimen/elements/ki-table'; import { defineCustomElement as defineCheckbox } from '@kimen/elements/ki-checkbox'; defineTable(); defineCheckbox(); ``` Apply sort requests and update the native header state from the page. ```js const frame = document.querySelector('#services'); const table = frame.querySelector('table'); frame.addEventListener('ki-sort', ({ detail: { key, direction } }) => { if (key !== 'name') return; const body = table.tBodies[0]; const nameOf = (row) => row.querySelector('th[scope="row"]').textContent.trim(); const sign = direction === 'ascending' ? 1 : -1; body.append(...Array.from(body.rows).sort((a, b) => sign * nameOf(a).localeCompare(nameOf(b)))); for (const header of table.tHead.querySelectorAll('th[data-sort]')) { if (header.dataset.sort === key) header.setAttribute('aria-sort', direction); else header.removeAttribute('aria-sort'); } }); frame.addEventListener('ki-selection-change', ({ detail: { keys } }) => { updateBulkActions(keys); }); ``` Use `density="compact"` where the available block space is tight. During a refresh, set `loading` to mark the native table busy and show a placeholder below the existing records. Remove it once the refresh ends. For a person column, place `` next to the visible name. For a row menu, use a trailing "Actions" header and a button whose name includes the row. Import `@kimen/elements/icons/ellipsis` before mounting the glyph. ```html View service ``` Give each row trigger a unique ID and handle the menu's `ki-select` event in the application. Translate the checkbox labels with `select-all-label="Sélectionner toutes les lignes"` and `row-selection-label="Sélectionner {row}"` on a French page.

components.docs: A tab group for switching between peer content views.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
switch between small sets of peer views inside the same page,
with one visible panel at a time. Use primary for the screen-level group
and secondary inside content.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
selecting form values
(use `ki-radio-group`), page navigation (use links), step flows, or
standalone `ki-tab` / `ki-tab-panel` children outside this group.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text:
- `ki-tab` and `ki-tab-panel` children. Tabs are auto-assigned to an
internal named slot as managed output.

docsTags.name: managedSlot
docsTags.text:
tab - The group stamps `slot="tab"` on its `ki-tab` children so
the tablist owns them; coordination, not authoring surface (spec 014).

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: tablist - Internal row around the tab strip: gap, alignment and the divider. The strip inside it carries the `tablist` role.

usage.examples:
Tabs pair with panels through a shared `value`; the group's `value` selects the active pair and `label` names the tablist:

```html
<ki-tabs label="Settings" value="email">
  <ki-tab value="email">Email</ki-tab>
  <ki-tab value="security">Security</ki-tab>
  <ki-tab-panel value="email">Email delivery preferences</ki-tab-panel>
  <ki-tab-panel value="security">Security and sign-in preferences</ki-tab-panel>
</ki-tabs>
```

A disabled tab stays visible but cannot be selected by any modality; user selection dispatches a composed `ki-change` event carrying the new value in `detail.value` (programmatic `value` writes stay silent):

```html
<ki-tabs label="Billing" value="plans">
  <ki-tab value="plans">Plans</ki-tab>
  <ki-tab value="invoices" disabled>Invoices</ki-tab>
  <ki-tab-panel value="plans">Plan management</ki-tab-panel>
  <ki-tab-panel value="invoices">Invoice history</ki-tab-panel>
</ki-tabs>
```

Use a primary group for tabs at screen level. In content, use
`variant="secondary"` for a full-width selection indicator. A decorative
SVG in a tab's `icon` slot stacks above the label in primary tabs and
appears before the label in secondary tabs. Set `icon-layout="inline"` or
`icon-layout="stacked"` to override the layout for the group.

```html
<ki-tabs label="Mail sections" variant="secondary">
  <ki-tab value="inbox">
    <svg slot="icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2">
      <path d="M3 5h18v14H3zM3 5l9 7 9-7" />
    </svg>
    Inbox
  </ki-tab>
  <ki-tab-panel value="inbox">Incoming messages</ki-tab-panel>
</ki-tabs>
```

props.name: iconLayout
props.docs:
Positions the decorative icon relative to its tab label. When omitted,
primary stacks the icon above the label and secondary puts it inline.

props.name: label
props.docs:
Accessible name for the tablist. Always provide one when multiple tab
groups may appear in a view. When NOT to use: do not use `label` as a
visible heading; render visible context in surrounding content.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: undefined

props.name: size
props.docs:
Token-backed strip size: every `ki-tab` it holds is 24, 32, 40, 48 or
56px tall in onmars, with its text, and the gap between tabs follows.
The strip decides for all its tabs; a tab has no size of its own. An
unrecognized value matches no style rule and keeps the medium metrics.
When to use: match the size of the controls around the strip.
When NOT to use: do not pick a smaller size to fit a dense region or a
larger one for touch; declare `data-ki-density` on the region instead,
which composes with every size.

docsTags.text: 'md'

components.docs:
A token-styled multiline text field with native form semantics.

Like a native field, it answers `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`,
`setCustomValidity(message)`, `validity`, `validationMessage` and
`willValidate` synchronously on a defined custom element.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
free-form text longer than one line, such as comments,
descriptions, messages, delivery notes, or addresses when paired with a
matching `autocomplete` purpose.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
single-line values (`ki-input`), constrained choices,
rich or formatted text editing, or search boxes.

Agent note: initial text is declared through the `value` attribute; element
text content is ignored. Enter inserts a line break and never submits the
enclosing form, the inverse of `ki-input`.

docsTags.name: part

error - Error line shown in place of the help text while the field is invalid
after the person answered or submitted; a polite live region, starting with a
decorative error symbol.

docsTags.name: part

label-hint - The `label-hint` text after the label text, inside the label and
part of the accessible name; rendered only while a hint is set.

docsTags.name: event
docsTags.text:
change - Fired when the user commits an edited value (on blur, with native
textarea timing), composed across the shadow boundary; `value` is already
current when listeners run. When to use: react to a committed value. When
NOT to use: do not use it for per-keystroke updates; the native `input`
event carries those.

usage.examples:
A labeled multiline field in a form (`label` is mandatory — the visible label and accessible name); `rows` sets the stable visible line count (default `2`, no auto-grow in v1):

```html
<form>
  <ki-textarea label="Comments" name="comments" rows="4"></ki-textarea>
  <ki-button variant="primary">Send</ki-button>
</form>
```

Initial text is declared through the `value` attribute — element text content is ignored — and Enter inserts a line break, never submitting the enclosing form:

```html
<ki-textarea label="Bio" name="bio" value="Web components enthusiast."></ki-textarea>
```

`required` blocks submission while empty, and an `autocomplete` purpose such as `street-address` exposes the entry's meaning to autofill:

```html
<ki-textarea
  label="Shipping address"
  name="address"
  rows="3"
  autocomplete="street-address"
  required
></ki-textarea>
```

Read-only and disabled are distinct states — `readonly` stays focusable, selectable, submitted and validation-exempt; `disabled` is none of those:

```html
<ki-textarea label="Accepted policy" value="Version 2.1, accepted 2026-05-02." readonly></ki-textarea>
<ki-textarea label="Legacy notes" value="Migrated from v1." disabled></ki-textarea>
```

## Appearance and character limits

Set `appearance` to `outlined` for a full border or `filled` for a
tinted surface with a bottom indicator. Both keep the label above the field.
The default appearance follows the theme.

`minlength` uses native minimum-length validation. The textarea keeps edits
past `maxlength` and blocks submission until the value fits. With a maximum,
`show-count` adds the current length to the field description and announces
when the user reaches or exceeds the limit. Use `maxlength-error-text` to
localize the default length error.

```html
<ki-textarea label="Bio" appearance="outlined" minlength="3" maxlength="24" show-count help-text="Keep it short" value="Designer and front-end developer"></ki-textarea>
<ki-textarea label="Short bio" appearance="filled" maxlength="12" show-count help-text="Keep it short" value="Designs generative interfaces."></ki-textarea>
```

## An error from the application

Set `custom-error` to show the application's verdict on the submitted text,
such as a moderation check. The field is invalid, blocks its form and is
announced as invalid at once. The person's next keystroke withdraws the
error. Remove the attribute when a new attempt starts: setting the same text
again while it is still set shows nothing.

```html
<ki-textarea label="Bio" name="bio" value="Call me at 555-0100" custom-error="Remove the phone number from your bio."></ki-textarea>
```

props.name: appearance
props.docs:
Field appearance. `default` uses the current theme, `outlined` draws a
full border, and `filled` uses a tinted surface and bottom indicator.
The visible label stays above the field.
When to use: set an explicit appearance when fields must share a shape
across themes.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: 'default'

props.name: autocomplete
props.docs:
Autofill detail token forwarded to the native textarea.
When to use: expose entry purpose such as `street-address` when available.
When NOT to use: omit when no valid autofill purpose applies.

props.name: customError
props.docs:
An error of the application's own, such as a server-side verdict on the
submitted text ("This title is taken"). While it holds text the field is
invalid, blocks its form, shows the text in place of the help text at
once and is announced as invalid. It stops counting at the person's next
change of the text, or when the form is reset, so it never blocks the
corrected answer. It outranks `error-text` and an error set with
`setCustomValidity`.
When to use: report a verdict from a declarative spec, a live update or a
framework binding. Remove it when a new attempt starts.
When NOT to use: do not use it for `required` or a length limit the field
enforces itself; `error-text` words those. Setting the same text again
while the prop still holds it shows nothing: remove it first, then set it
again.

props.name: disabled
props.docs:
Disables editing, focus, validation and form-data contribution.
When to use: make a field temporarily unavailable. When NOT to use: do not
use disabled for readonly review text that should submit.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: false

props.name: errorText
props.docs:
Message shown in place of the help text once the person's answer fails a
constraint (`required` or a length limit), and the field's `validationMessage`. Say how to
fix the answer. Without it the browser's own message shows, in the
browser's language. An error set with `custom-error` or
`setCustomValidity` outranks it.
When NOT to use: do not use it for server-side or cross-field errors; set
`custom-error` or call `setCustomValidity` for those.

props.name: helpText
props.docs:
One line of help under the field, read with it as its description: what
to write, or how long. While an error shows, the error takes its place.
When NOT to use: do not repeat the label, and do not use it for error
messages; use `error-text`.

props.name: label
props.docs:
Visible label rendered by the component and used as the accessible name.
When to use: always provide a concise label for the requested long-form
text. When NOT to use: do not substitute placeholder text for the label.

props.name: labelHint
props.docs:
Short text shown after the label and read with it as part of the field's
name, so people know before submitting whether to answer: "(optional)" on
the few optional fields of a mostly required form, or "(required)" the
other way round, in the page's own language. It changes no validation;
set `required` for that, and keep the two consistent.
When NOT to use: do not put instructions or length limits in it (use
`help-text`), errors (use `error-text`), or a repeat of the label.

props.name: maxlength
props.docs:
Soft maximum in UTF-16 code units. Longer user edits and assigned values
are preserved and fail form validation with `validity.tooLong`.
When to use: let people revise an over-limit draft without losing text.

props.name: maxlengthErrorText
props.docs:
Localized message for an over-limit value. `error-text` and
`setCustomValidity()` take precedence.
When to use: translate the soft maximum message for the page language.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: 'Shorten the text to fit the character limit.'

props.default: 'Shorten the text to fit the character limit.'

props.name: minlength
props.docs:
Native minimum length in UTF-16 code units for a nonempty user edit.
When to use: require a minimum number of characters in an answer.

props.name: name
props.docs:
Form-data key used when the textarea submits with a form.
When to use: provide for fields whose text must be included in FormData.
When NOT to use: omit for display-only or client-only fields.

props.name: placeholder
props.docs:
Hint shown while the textarea is empty.
When to use: add an example or short formatting hint. When NOT to use: do
not use placeholder as the accessible name or required instruction.

props.name: readonly
props.docs:
Makes the textarea focusable and selectable while rejecting edits.
When to use: show submitted or policy text that should still be included
in form data. When NOT to use: do not use readonly to remove a field from
submission; use disabled.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: false

props.name: required
props.docs:
Requires a non-empty value before form submission.
When to use: mark mandatory long-form text. When NOT to use: do not pair
with `readonly` expecting it to block; readonly fields are validation
exempt like native textareas.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: false

props.name: rows
props.docs:
Visible line count. Invalid, non-numeric, zero, or negative values fall
back to 2; no auto-grow or user resize handle exists in v1.
When to use: set the stable multiline height needed by the layout. When
NOT to use: do not use rows as a responsive size axis.

props.name: showCount
props.docs:
Shows the current count and maximum next to the help or error text and
announces reaching or exceeding the limit. Requires `maxlength`.
When to use: give people feedback while writing to a limit.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: false

props.name: size
props.docs:
Token-backed field size (`--ki-textarea-{size}-*` tokens): padding,
radius and text; the label and help text follow in three steps. The
height stays `rows` lines. An unrecognized value matches no style rule
and keeps the medium metrics.
When to use: match the size of the fields around it.
When NOT to use: do not pick a smaller size to fit a dense region or a
larger one for touch; declare `data-ki-density` on the region instead,
which composes with every size.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: 'md'

props.name: value
props.docs:
Live current text. The `value` attribute declares the reset default;
element text content is ignored. Programmatic assignments replace the
display and emit no events.
When to use: preload or read free-form text, line breaks included. When
NOT to use: do not put initial text between the element tags.

A time-of-day field with locale-aware typing and suggested slots. The shadow

usage.examples:
Display 12-hour time for a US English form and keep the value in canonical 24-hour form. The person can type any time from 08:00 through 18:00, including minutes between the half-hour suggestions. ```html ``` Set the language on a surrounding element to localize the time, and pass translated labels for the suggestion controls. Touch density increases the field and suggestion hit areas. ```html
``` ## An error from the application Set `custom-error` to show the application's verdict on the submitted time, such as a booking check. The field is invalid, blocks its form and is announced as invalid at once. The person's next edit or pick of a time withdraws the error. Remove the attribute when a new attempt starts: setting the same text again while it is still set shows nothing. ```html ```

props.name: customError
props.docs:
An error of the application's own, such as a server-side verdict on the
submitted time ("That slot was just booked"). While it holds text the
field is invalid, blocks its form, shows the text in place of the help
text at once and is announced as invalid. It stops counting at the
person's next edit or pick of a time, or when the form is reset, so it
never blocks the corrected answer. It outranks `error-text` and an error
set with `setCustomValidity`.
When to use: report a verdict from a declarative spec, a live update or a
framework binding. Remove it when a new attempt starts.
When NOT to use: do not use it for `required`, the bounds or unreadable
text, which the field reports itself; `error-text` words those. Setting
the same text again while the prop still holds it shows nothing: remove
it first, then set it again.

components.docs:
A short, transient message about something the person just did, shown
without blocking the page. It leaves on its own after its time, which stops
while the person points at the toaster, works inside it or is away from the
page; a toast with an action, or reporting an error, waits for the person.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
confirm an action that happened elsewhere on screen ("Changes
saved", "Link copied"), report a background result ("Export ready"), or
offer a quick undo. Raise it into a `ki-toaster`, in markup or with its
`show()` method; express urgency with `tone`.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
anything the person must read or act on to continue belongs
to `ki-dialog`; form validation belongs to the field's error text; a lasting
condition of the page belongs to `ki-alert`, which stays inline.

Assistive technology note: a toast announces as it appears, so append it
when the event happens; a toast present at initial page load is exposed with
its role but its announcement is not guaranteed. The heading and the message
are the whole announcement: the icon, the action and the dismiss button
stay outside the live region.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text: - Message text. It lives inside the live-region boundary.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text:
action - At most one action, as a `ki-button size="sm" variant="ghost"`.
Its own click handler runs, then the toast leaves (`reason: "action"`). A
toast holding an action never leaves on its own. When NOT to use: a response
the person cannot skip belongs in `ki-dialog`.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text:
toast - The flat surface: fill, image, edge, radius, padding,
elevation and backdrop filter.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: icon - The tone icon, drawn by the component in the tone's ink.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: heading - Optional bold first line, rendered only when non-empty.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: message - Message wrapper around the default slot.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: action - Wrapper around the `action` slot, rendered only when it holds content.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: dismiss - The dismiss `ki-icon-button`, rendered only when `dismissible`.

usage.examples:
Put a toast in a `ki-toaster` when something happens; it announces itself as it appears and leaves on its own after 5 seconds. `tone` picks the icon and its ink and the live-region urgency: `danger` exposes `role="alert"`, every other value `role="status"`:

```html
<ki-toaster>
  <ki-toast tone="success" heading="Changes saved">Workspace settings are up to date.</ki-toast>
</ki-toaster>
```

`duration` (milliseconds) changes the time; `0` keeps the toast until it is dismissed. A toast in the `danger` tone, or holding an action, never leaves on its own, whatever its `duration`. The time stops while the pointer rests on the toaster, while focus is inside it, or while the page is hidden:

```html
<ki-toast duration="8000">The export is ready in your downloads.</ki-toast>
<ki-toast tone="danger" heading="Upload failed">The file is larger than 20 MB.</ki-toast>
```

The `action` slot takes one ghost `ki-button size="sm"`. Its own click handler runs, then the toast leaves:

```html
<ki-toast heading="Message archived">
  The conversation moved to your archive.
  <ki-button slot="action" variant="ghost" size="sm">Undo</ki-button>
</ki-toast>
```

`ki-dismiss` says why the toast left: `detail.reason` is `"timeout"`, `"button"`, `"escape"` or `"action"`. `dismissible="false"` drops the dismiss button (Escape still works on a focused toast); `dismiss-label` is the component's only built-in word, so localize it whenever the document language is not English:

```html
<ki-toast lang="es" dismiss-label="Descartar">Borrador guardado.</ki-toast>
```

props.name: dismissLabel
props.docs:
Accessible name of the dismiss button. Override for localization; the
default English word is the component's only built-in text.

When to use: whenever the document language is not English.
When NOT to use: do not put the message here; use the default slot.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: 'Dismiss'

props.name: dismissed
props.docs:
Reflected state: true once the toast has left. The timer, the dismiss
button, Escape and the action set it; the page may set or clear it.
While true the host stays in the document but renders nothing and leaves
the accessibility tree. Clearing it shows the toast again with its full
time.

When to use: show a toast again, or close it from the page.
When NOT to use: do not read programmatic changes as dismissals;
`ki-dismiss` reports only the timer and the person.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: false

props.name: dismissible
props.docs:
Shows the dismiss button, a ghost `ki-icon-button` named by
`dismiss-label`. Escape still dismisses a focused toast without it.

When to use: keep it on unless the toast leaves on its own and the page
offers no other way to read it again.
When NOT to use: do not turn it off on a toast that waits for the person.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: true

props.name: duration
props.docs:
How long the toast stays, in milliseconds, before it leaves on its own;
`0` keeps it until it is dismissed. Ignored (treated as `0`) when the toast
holds an action or its tone is `danger`. Unset, or not a finite number of
zero or more, it is 5000. The time stops while the pointer rests on the
toaster, while focus is inside it, or while the page is hidden, and
continues with what was left. Changing it restarts the time.

When to use: give a longer message more time.
When NOT to use: do not shorten it below what a person needs to read the
message.

props.name: heading
props.docs:
Optional bold first line, inside the live region. Empty strings render no
heading. It is a `strong` element, never a document heading.

When to use: a short label for the event ("Changes saved").
When NOT to use: do not use it for page structure.

props.name: queued
props.docs:
Output-only state written by an enclosing `ki-toaster`: true while the
toast waits for a place. A queued toast renders nothing, is absent from
the accessibility tree and its time does not run. Authors do not set it;
the toaster overwrites it.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: false

props.name: tone
props.docs:
Picks the icon and its ink, and the live-region urgency: `danger` exposes
`role="alert"` and never leaves on its own; `neutral`, `info`, `success`,
`warning`, absent and unrecognized values expose `role="status"`. The
surface and the text look the same in every tone. Unknown values render
neutral.

When to use: choose the tone that describes what happened.
When NOT to use: do not use tone for emphasis; a lasting failure belongs
in `ki-alert`.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: 'neutral'

events.docs:
Fired once when the toast leaves because its time ran out
(`reason: "timeout"`), the person used the dismiss button (`"button"`),
pressed Escape inside it (`"escape"`) or activated its action
(`"action"`), after it is hidden and focus has been handed on. Not
cancelable. When to use: remove the element, or record that the message
was seen. When NOT to use: do not expect it for programmatic `dismissed`
changes.

components.docs:
The one place toasts appear: it paints its `ki-toast` children in the top
layer at a corner of the viewport, stacks them in arrival order, shows the
newest few and queues the older ones, without covering the page beside
them.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
once per page (or once inside a modal `ki-dialog`), as the place
every `ki-toast` of the application appears in: append toasts to it, or call
`show()`. Choose the corner with `placement`.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
do not put anything but `ki-toast` elements in it; do not use
it for persistent content, which belongs in the page or in `ki-alert`.

Assistive technology note: while it shows toasts the toaster is a group
named by `label`, never a landmark; F6 moves focus into it and Escape on a
toast returns focus to where it was. An empty toaster exposes nothing and
covers nothing.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text:
- The `ki-toast` elements, in arrival order. Other children are not
counted, queued or placed.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text:
stack - The stack in the top layer: placement, edge distance, gap
between toasts and width.

usage.examples:
Place one toaster per page (or one inside a modal `ki-dialog`). It paints its stack in the top layer, stacks toasts from the top down in arrival order and shows the newest three; older ones wait their turn:

```html
<ki-toaster></ki-toaster>
<script>
  document.querySelector('ki-toaster').show({
    tone: 'success',
    title: 'Changes saved',
    message: 'Workspace settings are up to date.',
    action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: undo },
  });
</script>
```

`show()` creates the toast, appends it, and removes it once it has left; its action renders as a ghost `ki-button size="sm"`. The toaster does not bundle either element, so define `ki-toast` and `ki-button` too. Toasts can also be written in markup inside the toaster; those stay the page's own and are never removed.

`placement` picks the corner — `top-center`, `top-end`, `bottom-center` or `bottom-end` (the default); `end` follows the writing direction, and a narrow touch screen always uses the bottom center. `max` sets how many toasts show at once:

```html
<ki-toaster placement="top-center" max="2"></ki-toaster>
```

While it shows toasts the toaster is a group named by `label` (`Notifications` by default); F6 moves focus into it, and Escape on a toast returns focus to where it was. Localize the name whenever the document language is not English:

```html
<ki-toaster lang="es" label="Avisos"></ki-toaster>
```

The distance from the viewport edges and the gap between toasts are tokens:

```css
:root {
  --ki-toaster-inset-block: 24px;
  --ki-toaster-inset-inline: 24px;
}
```

props.name: label
props.docs:
Accessible name of the group the toaster exposes while it shows toasts.
Override for localization.

When to use: provide the name in the document language.
When NOT to use: do not put a message here.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: 'Notifications'

props.name: max
props.docs:
How many toasts show at once: the newest ones. Older toasts wait, and come
back with their full time as shown ones leave. A toast holding focus keeps
its place until focus leaves the toaster; the oldest other one waits
instead. A value below 1 or not a whole number shows 3.

When to use: lower it on small screens or busy applications.
When NOT to use: do not raise it to show every toast; a tall stack covers
the page.

props.name: placement
props.docs:
Corner or edge of the viewport the stack sits against; `end` follows the
writing direction. On a coarse pointer and a viewport narrower than 40rem
the stack always sits at the bottom center. Unknown values place the stack
at the bottom end.

When to use: keep toasts away from where the page's own controls live.
When NOT to use: do not change it per toast; one toaster keeps one place.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: 'bottom-end'

methods.name: show
methods.docs:
Raises a toast: creates a `ki-toast` from `tone`, `title` (its heading),
`message`, `duration`, `dismissible` and `action` (a ghost
`ki-button size="sm"` in its `action` slot that calls `onClick`), appends
it to the toaster and resolves with it. Once the toast has left it is
removed from the page. The toaster does not bundle `ki-toast` or
`ki-button`: define them, as for toasts written in markup.
When to use: raise a toast from script without writing its markup.
When NOT to use: a toast written in markup stays the page's own: append
it instead, and it is never removed.

slots.docs:
The `ki-toast` elements, in arrival order. Other children are not
counted, queued or placed.

The stack in the top layer: placement, edge distance, gap
between toasts and width.

usage.examples:
# Toolbar examples

## Formatting controls

```html
<ki-toolbar label="Formatting">
  <ki-button variant="ghost">Bold</ki-button>
  <ki-divider orientation="vertical"></ki-divider>
  <ki-button variant="ghost">Insert link</ki-button>
</ki-toolbar>
```

Give icon-only actions their own label. With ToggleIconButton available, a
`ki-icon-button` with `toggle`, `selected` and `label="Bold"` owns the
pressed state and activation of the Bold command.

## Docked message actions

```html
<ki-toolbar label="Message actions" variant="docked" tone="vibrant" hide-on-scroll>
  <ki-button variant="ghost">Archive</ki-button>
  <ki-button variant="ghost">Mark unread</ki-button>
</ki-toolbar>
```

Reserve the bottom edge for the toolbar and leave space for its minimum
height plus `env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)` below page content. Use this
variant on compact pages without MobileNav.

## Floating with a FAB

When `ki-fab` is available, register it alongside the toolbar and buttons
when using direct imports. Give the FAB a label and use its named slot.

```html
<ki-toolbar label="Message actions" tone="vibrant">
  <ki-button variant="ghost">Archive</ki-button>
  <ki-fab slot="fab" label="Reply"></ki-fab>
</ki-toolbar>
```

This companion action follows the pill in the Tab sequence. Handle actions
on the slotted controls. The toolbar coordinates navigation and placement.

components.docs: A transient, text-only hint with an optional heading.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
add a brief clarifying hint for an icon-only, abbreviated, or
otherwise ambiguous control when the same information is discoverable
elsewhere in the interface.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
essential or unique information in a tooltip; interactive
content in a tooltip; form validation messages, disabled controls, or
touch-primary flows. Use visible layout text or a rich `ki-popover` with
`kind="toggletip"` when the content includes actions.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text:
- One trigger for a plain tooltip, or direct explanatory text when
`for` and `heading` are provided. Rich tooltips accept text only.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: tooltip - The non-focusable tooltip bubble.

usage.examples:
`label` is the entire plain tooltip content, reflected to the slotted trigger's accessible description; the trigger must already carry its own accessible name:

```html
<ki-tooltip label="Copies a shareable link to the clipboard">
  <ki-button type="button">Copy link</ki-button>
</ki-tooltip>
```

`placement` (default `top`; also `bottom`, `start`, `end`) is a preference — the component flips or clamps it to keep the bubble inside the viewport:

```html
<ki-tooltip label="Downloads the report as PDF" placement="bottom">
  <ki-button type="button">Export</ki-button>
</ki-tooltip>
```

An empty or whitespace-only `label` renders no tooltip and exposes no description — useful for conditional hints; never put essential or unique information in a tooltip:

```html
<ki-tooltip label="">
  <ki-button type="button">No hint here</ki-button>
</ki-tooltip>
```

Use a heading and direct text when the explanation needs more structure.
The external trigger must be in the same document or shadow tree.

```html
<button id="retention-info" type="button">Retention</button>
<ki-tooltip for="retention-info" heading="Grace period">
  Deleted projects stay restorable for 30 days.
</ki-tooltip>
```

For an explanation with controls, use `ki-popover` with
`kind="toggletip"` and `appearance="rich"`.

props.name: label
props.docs:
The entire plain tooltip content. The string is reflected to the slotted
trigger's accessible description without changing its name. Empty or
whitespace-only labels render no tooltip and expose no description.
When to use: a short hint that clarifies the slotted trigger.
When NOT to use: never use `label` for essential information, rich
content, interactive content, validation messages, or information attached
to disabled controls; put that content in visible UI or a popover.

props.name: placement
props.docs:
Preferred placement for the tooltip. The component may flip or clamp the
rendered placement to keep the bubble inside the viewport; unknown runtime
values fall back to `top`.
When NOT to use: do not depend on placement for meaning or reading order.

components.docs:
Application navigation with responsive primary links, or a per-screen app
bar with a real heading, optional search, and overflow actions.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
group a brand, up to five primary sections and global controls,
or set a screen title, leading control and screen actions in app-bar mode.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
more than five sections or a deep navigation tree (use a
sidebar), or switches between in-page views (use ki-tabs).

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text:
- Header mode: up to five direct native anchors; mark the current one with
aria-current="page". They stay the page's own anchors, so the page's link
rules reach them and outrank the bar's link styles (CSS Scoping gives the
page's styles precedence over a component's `::slotted()` rules, whatever
their specificity). `a { color: inherit }` is safe: the links then take the
bar's item ink. A rule that sets `color`, `text-decoration`, `font-*` or
`padding` on every `a` restyles them too: scope it away from the bar, for
example `:where(main, footer) a` or `a:not(ki-top-nav > a)`, and restyle the
bar's links with the `--ki-top-nav-item-*` tokens.

usage.examples:
# Using TopNav ## Application header Use direct anchors for primary sections and keep the page's skip link before the header. Import `@kimen/elements/icons/bell` for the notification glyph. ```html Skip to content Kimen Overview Projects
Workspace
``` ## Links that wrap instead of collapsing Use `collapse-at="none"` to keep every link in the bar at every width. When space runs out, the brand and actions keep the first row, and the links wrap across the full width below. Tab reaches the actions after the links. Use `--ki-top-nav-links-gap` for the column gap and `--ki-top-nav-links-justify: flex-end` to align the links with the trailing edge of their available space. ```html Kimen Design System Guide Components Tokens ``` ## Per-screen bar with search Use the native `title` attribute in HTML and `screenTitle` for the framework prop. The leading button and search control keep their names and behavior. The screen heading remains accessible when search occupies its visual space. ```html ``` When an app bar has more than three actions, slot the named controls directly. Attach handlers to those controls. TopNav uses their existing activation handlers in the overflow menu. Keep application-specific account menus and navigation destinations in the consuming app.

usage.examples:
# Tree examples

Give the tree a label and put the item text before any nested items. Set
`expanded` to show a branch's children and `selected` to mark the initial
selection. The tree defaults to single selection.

```html
<ki-tree label="Project files">
  <ki-tree-item expanded>
    src
    <ki-tree-item selected>ki-dialog.ts</ki-tree-item>
    <ki-tree-item>ki-menu.ts</ki-tree-item>
  </ki-tree-item>
  <ki-tree-item>README.md</ki-tree-item>
</ki-tree>
```

Set `selection="multiple"` to show checkboxes. The Reports branch starts
mixed because Summary is the only checked child. Toggling Reports also
updates its enabled descendants. The `ki-selection-change` event reports
the committed selection in `detail.selectedItems`, including fully checked
branches.

```html
<ki-tree label="Export files" selection="multiple">
  <ki-tree-item expanded>
    Reports
    <ki-tree-item selected>Summary</ki-tree-item>
    <ki-tree-item>Appendix</ki-tree-item>
    <ki-tree-item disabled>Draft</ki-tree-item>
  </ki-tree-item>
</ki-tree>
```

Use `selection="none"` with `href` to build a navigation tree.

```html
<ki-tree label="Documentation" selection="none">
  <ki-tree-item expanded>
    Guides
    <ki-tree-item href="./quick-start/">Quick start</ki-tree-item>
    <ki-tree-item href="./theming/">Theming</ki-tree-item>
  </ki-tree-item>
</ki-tree>
```

A lazy branch emits `ki-load` the first time it opens. Append its child
items to `event.detail.item` to replace the spinner. Set `item.lazy = false`
to finish the wait if there are no children.

```html
<ki-tree label="Project files">
  <ki-tree-item lazy loading-label="Loading tokens">tokens</ki-tree-item>
</ki-tree>
```

```js
document.querySelector('ki-tree')?.addEventListener('ki-load', ({ detail: { item } }) => {
  const child = document.createElement('ki-tree-item');
  child.textContent = 'palette.tokens.json';
  item.append(child);
});
```

usage.examples:
# Tree item examples

Place each item directly in a `ki-tree` or another `ki-tree-item`. Put the
label text before the child items. A disabled item stays in the tree's
arrow-key sequence and cannot be activated.

```html
<ki-tree label="Project files">
  <ki-tree-item expanded>
    src
    <ki-tree-item selected>ki-dialog.ts</ki-tree-item>
    <ki-tree-item disabled>Archived code</ki-tree-item>
  </ki-tree-item>
</ki-tree>
```

Import the decorative glyph before the tree mounts if you set `icon-name`.

```js
import '@kimen/elements/icons/file-code';
```

```html
<ki-tree label="Project files">
  <ki-tree-item icon-name="file-code">ki-dialog.ts</ki-tree-item>
</ki-tree>
```

components.docs:
A themed video surface: a calm poster facade with exactly one accessible
play control over a slotted native `<video>` element. From the first
activation on, playback, scrubbing, volume, captions and fullscreen belong
to the native player — Kimen ships no custom chrome.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
playable content the person deliberately chooses to watch —
product tours, talks, tutorials, announcements — presented as a poster
with one play control. Slot exactly one native `<video>` carrying its own
`poster`, sources and `<track>` captions, omit `controls` (the component
enables the native chrome the moment the facade yields, FR-002), and give
the control a `label` (required: the accessible name of the play button).

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
decorative background or ambient loops (plain CSS and
`<video>` are the tool), audio-only recordings (use ki-audio),
embeds from streaming platforms that ship their own player chrome (use
their embed), or static imagery (use an image, not a video). `autoplay`
on the slotted media is unsupported: the facade's contract is that
playback begins only by explicit user activation — never on scroll,
hover or visibility — so preexisting `autoplay` and `controls` on the
slotted media are cleared when it arrives, and any playback already
running is paused (FR-003; the native chrome returns at activation).

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text: - Exactly one native `<video>` element carrying its own poster, sources and `<track>` captions.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: frame - The media frame: radius, clipping, the themed surface.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: play - The play control: overlay scrim, glass container and glyph.

usage.examples:
Slot exactly one native `<video>` carrying its own poster, sources and `<track>` captions; `label` names the play control (required — never rendered visually) and the native chrome returns the moment the facade yields:

```html
<ki-video label="Play the product tour">
  <video muted playsinline width="1280" height="720" poster="tour.jpg">
    <source src="tour.webm" type="video/webm" />
    <track kind="captions" srclang="en" label="English" src="tour.en.vtt" />
  </video>
</ki-video>
```

Everything on the media element passes through untouched — offer format fallbacks through multiple `<source>` children, and the native media events (`play`, `pause`, `ended`) keep firing on the element you own; ki-video emits no events of its own:

```html
<ki-video label="Play the setup walkthrough">
  <video width="1280" height="720" poster="walkthrough.jpg">
    <source src="walkthrough.webm" type="video/webm" />
    <source src="walkthrough.mp4" type="video/mp4" />
    <track kind="captions" srclang="en" label="English" src="walkthrough.en.vtt" />
  </video>
</ki-video>
```

The frame fills its container's inline size and the media keeps the intrinsic aspect ratio declared by `width`/`height` (16:9 is a demonstration, not a constraint); `autoplay` and `controls` on arriving media are cleared — playback begins only from the play control:

```html
<ki-video label="Play the workshop recording">
  <video width="800" height="600" poster="workshop.jpg">
    <source src="workshop.mp4" type="video/mp4" />
    <track kind="captions" srclang="en" label="English" src="workshop.en.vtt" />
  </video>
</ki-video>
```

props.name: label
props.docs:
Accessible name of the play control ("Play the product tour"). The
control is a real button exposing role button with exactly this name;
the frame contributes no role, name or state of its own (FR-004,
FR-005). Documented as required: no default human-language string is
baked in, and an unlabeled control renders but fails the accessibility
audit (015-ki-progress precedent). The label is never rendered visually.
